QPR man will be playing in the Premier League next season, believes EFL expert

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, QPR swooped to sign the stopper on loan from Manchester City in the summer.
  • Charles, 21, has made 17 appearances for the Hoops in all competitions to date this season, 16 of which have come in the league, and he has kept four clean sheets.
  • Recent findings suggest that maxwell has delivered his verdict on Charles on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “In terms of a goalkeeper’s passing range and ability, I’ve quite simply never seen anything like this with Charles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, QPR swooped to sign the stopper on loan from Manchester City in the summer. He has since become the Hoops’ number one and has made a positive impression with the London outfit in the Championship.

Charles, 21, has made 17 appearances for the Hoops in all competitions to date this season, 16 of which have come in the league, and he has kept four clean sheets. The R’s are right now in the play-offs along with Wolves, Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton and Swansea City, with the likes of West Ham and Sheffield United chasing them down.

Recent findings suggest that maxwell has delivered his verdict on Charles on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “In terms of a goalkeeper’s passing range and ability, I’ve quite simply never seen anything like this with Charles. We’re talking about dropping passes wherever he wants, on a dime, on a sixpence, with both feet, on different trajectories.”.

He added: “We really need to enjoy him while we can, I don’t think he’ll be playing in the Championship after this season. Player like this are genuinely the reason why you fall in love with the game.”.

QPR’s decision to bring in Charles in the last transfer window has worked out well for them. He has settled into life with the Hoops well and has become their first choice.

According to recent reports, the Northern Ireland international, who has 18 caps to his name, was on the books at Sheffield Wednesday from 2021 to 2026. He went on to play 36 matches for the Owls, 21 of which came in the last campaign.

It has been revealed that charles was snapped up by Manchester City on a long-term deal in July. He was then given the green light to head out the exit door on a temporary basis to join the R’s.

Sources indicate that city will be pleased with his development under Julien Stephan. He has enjoyed plenty of game time at QPR and is getting plenty of valuable experience under his belt.

It has been revealed that charles’ ability with the ball at his feet makes him the perfect modern day goalkeeper. At the age of just 21 still, he has potential to get even better down the line.

In a recent development, QPR should savour him while they can this term as they eye promotion to the top flight. Manchester City will have a big decision to make on what to do with him when he returns to the Etihad Stadium.

According to recent reports, if the Hoops go up, they will fancy their chances of re-signing him again. If they stay in the EFL though, it seems unlikely he would come back for a second spell.

Stephan’s side won 1-0 away at Millwall last time out with Nicolas Madsen getting their winner against the Lions at The Den in the first-half. They are back in action on Tuesday with an away trip to Norwich City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan are thinking about bolstering their academy with the Malmö FF talent Leon Da Silva, according to a report.

In recent months, a lot of focus has been on how Milan will reinforce the first team in January and next summer. Understandably so, as Gerry Cardinale seemingly has big spending aims, keen on making it back to the Champions League next season.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, amidst all of the first-team rumours, however, Milan are also working on the academy. Jovan Kirovski is evaluating players for the Futuro side with his team, while Vincenzo Vergine (pictured) and his team are doing so for the Primavera and below.

In a recent development, according to Gianluca Di Marzio, one of the players on Milan’s wish list is Leon Da Silva, who at the moment plays in the academy of Malmö FF. At the age of 16, he’s yet to make his debut with the first team, but he did feature in a friendly game last month.

It has been revealed that da Silva plays as a centre-back and as the report states, he has even been compared to Virgil Van Dijk for how he plays. Since he’s still very young, if Milan were to secure his services, he would start with the Primavera team (or even in the younger sides).

In addition to Milan, the likes of Inter and Torino are also monitoring the Swede, though it seems Malmö are keen on keeping him for a few more years.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, according to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position.
  • Industry observers note that alexandersson is at the moment the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, swansea City are pursuing a latest head coach after Vitor Matos left his role at the Swansea.com Stadium to take charge of RC Strasbourg. Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O’Leary are leading the Swans on an interim basis, but ground is quickly being made in the search for a new boss.

According to recent reports, according to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position. Talks have been held between the 44-year-old and the Championship club, and he appears to be their prime target at present.

Industry observers note that alexandersson is at the moment the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June. He has overseen 14 wins in his 19 games in charge of the club, recording a points-per-game rate of 2.32.

Alexandersson is a 44-year-old coach who has held a variety of roles in the dugout since beginning his coaching career back in 2008. He spent seven years at Leiknir Reykjavik as a player before moving into management.

Industry observers note that the Swansea City target started out in women’s football, managing club team Valur before a short spell in charge of former club Leiknir Reykjavik. Alongside this role, Alexandersson spent five years as manager of the Iceland women’s national side.

It has been revealed that he then stepped into the men’s setup as an assistant to Erik Hamren and Arnar Vidarsson before a short spell as a No. 2 at Al-Arabi. From 2021 though, Alexandersson has worked strictly as a first-team boss in men’s football.

Industry observers note that he spent nearly three years in charge of Danish side Lyngby BK and 11 months at KV Kortrijk in Belgium before moving to SK Brann in Norway. Impressive work there saw him poached for the Rosenborg BK job, where he has continued to impress.

Swansea City head coach contender Alexandersson prioritises man management, working closely with his players to build strong relationships and placing importance on leadership. He has a strong reputation for developing players, which will appeal to the Swans too.

Tactically, his Rosenborg side set up in a 4-3-3 primarily, but he has used 5-3-2 or 3-5-2 formations in the past. Much like Matos, his teams press aggressively in the final third, and he demands frequent chance creation with players directed to suffocate opponents on and off the ball.

According to recent reports, in terms of tactical similarities, Alexandersson feels like a great fit for Swansea City. The fact he wants his players to press high and play forwards much like Matos means that there can be a smooth transition into the newly introduced management.

Bringing in a boss with completely different ideas could bring teething problems. This squad has been built to play on the front foot with and without the ball, and Alexandersson will ensure they do so.

The Jamestown Analytics influence feels clear with this pursuit. They pride themselves on finding gems in lesser-used markets, and Alexandersson could be the latest top boss uncovered.

After initial talks, time will tell whether the Swans can strike a deal to bring Alexandersson to Wales.

Jürgen Klopp has an unexpected connection to West Ham’s January looks

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1069 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite a change in the dugout, West Ham’s woes in the Championship have continued.
  • Scott Parker is yet to taste victory since taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, with a 1-1 draw at home to bottom of the table Preston North End last weekend typifying their early-season struggles.
  • The Hammers now sit 10th in the second tier standings after 16 league games, with it difficult to see when and how the East London outfit are going to get back on an upward trajectory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite a change in the dugout, West Ham’s woes in the Championship have continued.

Scott Parker is yet to taste victory since taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, with a 1-1 draw at home to bottom of the table Preston North End last weekend typifying their early-season struggles.

The Hammers now sit 10th in the second tier standings after 16 league games, with it difficult to see when and how the East London outfit are going to get back on an upward trajectory.

One way could be to address certain positions in the January transfer window, but yet again, there are so many games to come in a congested winter period, so it’s important that from somewhere, West Ham find a bit of magic to keep themselves in the promotion mix.

A position West Ham have really struggled with so far this season is the lack of a clinical frontman, with none of Taty Castellanos, Joel Piroe or Pablo contributing enough on a consistent basis.

Meanwhile, one forward they let go of in the summer, Niclas Füllkrug, is enjoying such a fruitful spell back in Germany on loan at Werder Bremen, so much so he’s earned recognition from national team manager Jürgen Klopp.

Such a rise back to form may give the Hammers an interesting decision to make in January as to whether they get the forward back in the fold or sell him for a sizeable fee at the turn of the fresh year.

Niclas Füllkrug arrived at West Ham with quite the reputation.

After netting 15 and assisting 10 in all competitions for Borussia Dortmund in the 2023-24 campaign, he followed that up with a couple of goals for Germany in Euro 2024, peaking the Hammers’ interest.

West Ham thought they were bringing such goalscoring prowess to England following the tournament, spending £27 million to sign the then-31-year-old, but his time at the London Stadium was nothing short of disastrous.

Füllkrug’s first season at the club was marred by injuries, with the German starting just six times and scoring three goals in the process.

Last year, he made just eight league appearances before being deemed surplus to requirements and loaned out to AC Milan, where he scored just once in under 650 minutes of football.

It wasn't exactly a spell which warranted a return to the West Ham fold ahead of a Championship return, and the 33-year-old was loaned back to Werder Bremen during the summer, with it expected that he'd see out the final two years of his Hammers contract elsewhere.

Many connected with West Ham will be amazed at the turnaround Niclas Füllkrug has made on his return to Germany, demonstrating himself to be one of the most lethal finishers in the Bundesliga this season.

Füllkrug has found his form back in familar surroundings, with his last campaign with Bremen in 2022-23 resulting in a 16-goal return,.

But the 33-year-old is well on his way to surpassing that number, netting 10 goals in as many appearances so far in the German top-flight.

West Ham fans, can you quite believe Niclas Füllkrug's revival at Werder Bremen? Comment your thoughts below!

Füllkrug is right now the top scorer in the division, one ahead of Bayer Leverkusen’s Patrik Schick and six ahead of Ballon D’Or winner Harry Kane in an unprecedented revival.

With Niclas Füllkrug banging in goals for fun and his confidence sky-high, there was no surprise to see him raise eyebrows on the national front.

And at the start of November, a report by German outlet Kicker revealed that the Werder Bremen frontman had been recalled to the national team by Jürgen Klopp for their Nations League fixtures against Serbia and the Netherlands.

Klopp was very complimentary of Füllkrug’s form too, saying: "Good form and scoring goals are never a bad thing.

"Fülle has been performing and scoring all kinds of goals, almost all of them spectacular. He has an incredible influence on Werder Bremen, not just through his goals, but also through the way he carries himself.".

Such impressive words from Klopp are testament to the impact Füllkrug has had on his return to Germany, and it leaves West Ham with a major decision to make as the January transfer window ticks down.

Füllkrug remains contracted to the Hammers as he’s only on a season-long loan at Bremen, but Werder’s managing director, Clemens Fritz, has publicly expressed interest in signing the striker permanently, although he stressed that any agreement must involve all three parties of Bremen, West Ham and the player.

The West Ham faithful will be bemoaning the fact Niclas Füllkrug failed to show much goalscoring ability at the London Stadium, but then returning to Germany has him placed as one of the league’s top performing players.

And while their association with the German frontman on the pitch has been a complete waste of time, there could be some light at the end of the tunnel as to how much money they can get for him.

Despite having just two years left on his contract, Werder Bremen clearly value Füllkrug highly given the impact he’s made on his return, and with their managing director already showing his interest in making the Weserstadion Füllkrug's home again on a permanent basis, it’s evidence enough that the German outfit would be willing to pay quite a lot of money to keep hold of the Bundesliga’s top scorer.

Werder Bremen are believed to not have an option to buy in the original loan deal, so the ball is very much in West Ham’s court when it comes to negotiating terms.

The Hammers must stand firm when it comes to a price, with the club having to hold out to get as much back on the £27m deal they signed off to bring him to the London Stadium in the first place.

Praying on Werder Bremen’s desperation, such a lump of cash could have a significant say on their January transfer aims, with much of that money being used to bring in a upcoming striker that could help turn the Hammers’ fortunes around and still have them in contention for a place back in the Premier League.

So while much of Füllkrug's stint at West Ham has been filled with bitter disappointment, it could end up having the perfect ending and playing a huge part in Scott Parker’s men achieving their promotion dreams in May.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that so it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

Recent findings suggest that so it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o.

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he mentioned. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”.

What an crucial week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

It has been revealed that the key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” noted Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

8 players set to miss Sheffield United v Southampton

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sheffield United host high-flying Southampton at Bramall Lane on Tuesday night, as both sides will be aiming to maintain their positive run of form in this thrilling clash.
  • Sheffield United, after a tricky summer transfer window and subsequent tricky run of results, have turned their form around to become outside shouts of a play-off spot this season, with four wins, one draw, and one defeat in their last six Championship games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield United host high-flying Southampton at Bramall Lane on Tuesday night, as both sides will be aiming to maintain their positive run of form in this thrilling clash.

Sheffield United, after a tricky summer transfer window and subsequent tricky run of results, have turned their form around to become outside shouts of a play-off spot this season, with four wins, one draw, and one defeat in their last six Championship games.

Head coach Chris Wilder will certainly have his focus set on a place in the top eight this campaign, but if the Blades are to have any realistic chance of doing so, claiming all three points when they host Southampton on Tuesday would go a long way.

The Saints are on an excellent run of form themselves, with five wins, two draws, and one defeat in their last eight games as well, climbing from -4 points up to 6th in the table after 16 games.

Under the lights in South Yorkshire, it's shaping up to be a tense affair, as Football League World takes a closer look at the players set to miss out on this clash.

Japhet Tanganga is the first of numerous absentees from Tuesday's fixture at Bramall Lane, with the former Tottenham Hotspur set to sit the game out through suspension after picking up five yellow cards.

13 players were booked in Sheffield United's 4-0 home win over Watford at the weekend, including Tanganga, as Mark McGuinness or Jamal Baptiste will likely step in during the 27-year-old's absence.

Not injured and not suspended - Ben Brereton Diaz will not be allowed to face Southampton on Tuesday night due to EFL rules dictating that he cannot play against his parent club, having returned to South Yorkshire for a third separate spell this summer from St Mary's.

Wilder will be forced to mix up his attack, with Tom Cannon, Tyrese Campbell, and Patrick Bamford vying for a place in the Blades' starting XI.

English right-back Femi Seriki is to face a year on the sidelines after suffering a serious knee injury six minutes after coming on as a substitute in the Blades' 2-1 away defeat to Charlton Athletic.

Wilder described the 23-year-old's absence for the next 12 months or so as a 'hammer blow', and in his place, Hamza Choudhury will likely retain his place at right-back, with another option in that area also set to miss this fixture against Southampton.

Since joining Sheffield United on a free transfer in the summer, Irish defender Matt Doherty has managed just 41 minutes of league football for the Blades, having frequently appeared as an unused substitute this campaign.

Wilder has confirmed that he expects the Irishman to be available before the end of the year, but is set to miss this one, with the Blades gaffer saying: "Hopefully, he'll be available before January. We've got five weeks left of that, so maybe mid-December he'll be available for selection.".

Scottish striker Ryan One has found minutes in South Yorkshire difficult to come by following his positive loan spell in League One with Lincoln City last season, managing just 30 minutes of Championship football at this stage.

It has been revealed that on One's return to action, Wilder remarked: "He’s about a month or 6 weeks away. So, I think the start of 2027, he’ll be back. We're going to have to take a little bit more time with him. That's not that we overwhelmed him or pushed him too hard. We didn't, but we're just going to have to take that little bit more extra time on him now to make sure there's not a recurrence of the injury.".

Former Blackburn Rovers, Bournemouth, and Leeds United midfielder Joe Rothwell has found minutes at Bramall Lane difficult to come by since joining in January 2026, with just over 400 minutes of league football this season.

Industry observers note that wilder confirmed before the most recent international break that the Englishman was to undergo a minor operation on an injury, saying: "Joe's got to have a minor op that's going to keep him out until after the international break. So he might miss the Watford and Southampton games.".

Onto the Southampton players set to miss this one, and the list looks much more positive for the Saints than it does for the home side, though with German defender Keven Schlotterbeck to miss this one, it's not all rosy on the South Coast.

The 29-year-old has made 13 Championship appearances for the club since his summer move from Augsburg, replacing the outgoing Taylor Harwood-Bellis, but having dislocated his shoulder against Preston North End, he is not expected to be back in action until at least December, with Zach Abbott likely to retain his place in the heart of the Saints back line.

Who do you think will be the biggest miss in this fixture, and what are your score predictions? Share your thoughts below!

Schlotterbeck's compatriot and teammate Casper Jander has been blighted with injuries this campaign, making just three league appearances throughout October before missing the most recent chunk of games.

It has been revealed that when asked about Jander, Southampton boss Tonda Eckert mentioned: "He'll be back this week. I'm not 100 per cent sure if we have him on Tuesday. I'm hopeful that we have him on Tuesday, but he'll be back this week.".

There is a chance the former Nuremberg midfielder will make the cut for this away trip to Sheffield United, though it's more likely he will be back next weekend for Middlesbrough at home.

Italy U21 coach discusses Cisse’s rise, next steps for Camarda and why Bartesaghi is ‘a luxury’

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (918 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.
  • According to recent reports, in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.

According to recent reports, in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team. Bartesaghi was the first to properly get in, cementing his spot in the starting eleven last season, while Cisse has been the big breakthrough this season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Camarda has had a tougher time after a loan spell at Lecce, but Milan have made it very clear through renewals and words that they will focus more on the youngsters. It’s exciting times as well, given how they have all performed with the U21 national team too.

It has been revealed that speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Italy’s U21 coach Silvio Baldini was asked about the breakthrough of Cisse, Camarda’s current state of mind and why Bartesaghi is a ‘luxury’ for his team. Safe to say that he likes the trio a lot.

Cisse has had a proper breakthrough. Did you see that coming?

“Compared to a year ago, I can see a different guy, who’s more mature and prepared, with higher self-esteem, psychologically changed, simply stronger.

Industry observers note that “He has Milan to thank for signing him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and making room for him, then giving him consistent playing time. If he then makes the national team and does well, so much the better.”.

Milan deserve credit, and you also deserve credit for discovering him as a centre-forward….

Industry observers note that “Analysing training sessions, a series of situations emerged where he managed to score by attacking space and depth: if you can do it on the right and left, it means you can also do it in the centre. But even there, the credit goes entirely to the staff.

Sources indicate that “They had the intuition, realising that Cisse could be useful to our game system in that way and at the same time, allowing Alpha to discover a latest role successfully. I’m simply honest and meritocratic in my choices.

“Even though the goal against Armenia actually came from him as a second striker, at the end of that match we had two centre-forwards, him and Camarda.”.

According to recent reports, camarda, by the way, has struggled at Milan but scored for the U21s. How is that possible?

Industry observers note that “I can only speak about the work we do together. I spoke to him at length, I dedicated time to him, I asked him to explain his concerns, his fear of not being able to express himself as he would like. I told him stories of my own life, of how I came out of it.

“A dialogue not as a coach-player but as a son, or rather a grandson, as he could be, and a grandfather: from the heart. I’m not interested in performances as an end in themselves; they will come if he feels in the right place.

“I try to make him understand that I see him, I follow him in many small ways: he’s a conscientious boy who shouldn’t become obsessed with the goal, but rather experience football for what it is: fun.

“If, instead of fun, it becomes a test, then it worries you, and if you worry, you no longer enjoy it and it doesn’t help you perform at your best.”.

To have more fun, do you recommend that he should leave Milan for another team?

It has been revealed that “I’m not going to get involved in this. There are clubs, agents, and a family: they know what the best path will be for him. Let’s remember that he’s 18 years old, he plays for AC Milan and in the Under-21s.

It has been revealed that “It’s clear that the more he plays, the better it will be for AC Milan and for everyone. We’re talking about a great player, a champion in my opinion, who needs to finish his development: he’s still growing, he already has a great eye for goal, and he’s sacrificing himself for the team.”.

Camarda-Cisse: Can Milan provide the national team with one of the forward duos of the future?

According to recent reports, “For me, yes. I see them as a permanent fixture in the national team, and of course they need to prove it and earn it on the pitch. But they have all the characteristics to do it. I found Alpha to be better prepared, even in his game decisions. Amorim did well to develop him.”.

The third Rossoneri player is Bartesaghi: more of a full-back like with you or a winger like at Milan?

“Davide is one of the best players in his position I’ve coached in many years. He’s talented, very professional, mature, introverted yet open, and that’s not a contradiction: he has enormous potential, and he shows it every time he comes to us.

It has been revealed that “If I were any Serie A coach, I’d take him with me. For the Under-21s, Bartesaghi is a luxury. He plays with heart, passion, and intelligence, as well as possessing high-level technical, physical, and running skills.

In a recent development, “He can play in any position on the flank. In my opinion, if he starts 50 meters from the goal, he can perform at his best.”.

Manchester United are not expected to stand in his way if a suitable opportunity to leave comes, especially following his public criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

In a recent development, the defender is out of contract at the end of the season, although United have the option to trigger a further 12 months. Whether the club chooses to use that clause remains to be seen.

Industry observers note that A departure from Manchester United could give Martinez the chance to find a new challenge after four seasons in Manchester. Barcelona had looked like a possible destination, but the latest reports suggest they are not right now pushing for his signature.

Lisandro Martinez’s hopes of joining Barcelona appear to have suffered a major setback, with reports from Spain claiming that neither sporting director Deco nor manager Hansi Flick is convinced by the Manchester United defender.

Atletico Madrid had also been mentioned among the interested clubs but there weren’t any further reports on a possible transfer, leaving Martínez’s options in Spain uncertain.

The latest claims suggest a switch to the Camp Nou may be unlikely.

“Lisandro, as far as I’m aware, neither Deco nor Flick are keen on him,” Bravo was quoted as saying.

The journalist also claimed to have spoken directly with Deco, who is also ruled Martinez out.

“He’s a good player, but we don’t like him. He doesn’t fit in with us.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.
  • His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.
  • It has been revealed that pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

It has been revealed that pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches. He has a massive job ahead of him, with many pundits and former players terming his situation the toughest in the Premier League.

Gary Neville believes the Argentine will need several transfer windows to get the squad where he wants it, if he gets that much of time at Manchester United.

The former captain shared his views on which players he expects Pochettino to keep, and who could be heading for the exit.

According to recent reports, neville believes Senne Lammens should remain part of the plans, although he expects Pochettino to bring in another goalkeeper to give him some competition for his place. At the back, he backed Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro to stay, while suggesting Ayden Heaven needs a loan move to the Championship.

“Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in,” Neville noted on Stick to Football.

In midfield, Neville wants Pochettino to build around Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. He also believes Andrey Santos could have a future at the club because of his age, mobility and aggression.

In a recent development, mason Mount, however, is not part of his looks. Neville remarked: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.

Neville also has his doubts on the forward line, with much of the front line seeing a change. Gary Neville expects Joshua Zirkzee to leave and believes United cannot continue paying Marcus Rashford’s wages.

“Zirkzee definitely to go. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.”.

It has been revealed that he expects Pochettino to work with Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. Patrick Dorgu could also be useful in the short term, although Neville thinks he may leave within the next couple of years. Manuel Ugarte, meanwhile, was another player he was certain would go.

Recent findings suggest that talking about the exits, Gary Neville has singled out many United stars to be shown the door in the first wave of squad clearance by Mauricio Pochettino. Neville identified Lisandro Martínez, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui as further candidates to leave in the first wave of departures, alongside Mount, Rashford and Zirkzee.

Neville believes another group of exits could follow a year later, with Shaw, Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Fernandes among the players whose futures may not be at the club in long term. Pochettino would also have to decide whether Santos and Carlos Baleba fit into his long-term aims.

Neville does not expect United to rebuild the squad in a single summer, even if Pochettino makes a positive start.

“But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.”.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

Andre's Wolves future has a 2031 twist amid Cesar Peixoto's January warning

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Wolves are starting to build momentum as they target an immediate return to the Premier League under Cesar Peixoto.
  • The Black Country outfit were always expected to be in the mix for promotion due to the quality of the squad they boast after eight years in the Premier League.
  • Whilst there was a feeling that Wolves could’ve spent more in the summer, they did manage to retain several key players, and the likes of Ladislav Krejčí and Andre are emerging as huge figures for Peixoto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wolves are starting to build momentum as they target an immediate return to the Premier League under Cesar Peixoto.

The Black Country outfit were always expected to be in the mix for promotion due to the quality of the squad they boast after eight years in the Premier League.

Whilst there was a feeling that Wolves could’ve spent more in the summer, they did manage to retain several key players, and the likes of Ladislav Krejčí and Andre are emerging as huge figures for Peixoto.

The latter has started every Championship game this season, which speaks volumes to his importance when you consider how often Peixoto has rotated.

Yet, he recognises the qualities that Andre brings, and the reality is that even though Wolves have some good midfield options on the bench, the Brazilian is easily the strongest defensive midfielder in the squad.

Therefore, it will come as no surprise that Peixoto has already warned Wolves against selling the former Fluminense man in the New Year, as he told the club’s media that a sale must not be on the agenda.

Industry observers note that “I don’t need to say how key he is for us. We have to keep him with us until the end of the season. He’s a very, very important player, a key player for us.

According to recent reports, “I hope, and I expect, that he stays with us. In my head, I don’t want to hear anything about Andre leaving. It is impossible to be clearer than that. For sure, there’ll be interest in him in January as he’s a great player, but he’s our player, and he’s going to stay with us.”.

Following on from that, you could make a strong case that Andre is the most notable player in the Wolves squad right now.

Such is the strength in depth at Molineux, Wolves have two players for every position, and they’ve coped reasonably well without Raul Jimenez for a chunk of the campaign already.

Boubacar Traore is a decent backup to Andre, but he doesn’t possess the same attributes as the 25-year-old, and his fitness is a concern as well.

Sources indicate that at his best, Andre is the man who makes things tick for Wolves. He plays with real intensity in shutting down the opposition, and his tactical understanding of the game ensures he is always in the right place. Then, on the ball, he is effective at moving it swiftly, and he is capable of switching play.

Andre also relishes the physical side of the Championship, and his presence in the middle of the park is a major factor in why Wolves have the best xG against in the division.

Peixoto’s comments about Andre were understandable, as there will be interest in the midfielder, but the pleasing thing for Wolves is that they hold all the cards when it comes to negotiations.

That’s because, to the shock of many, Andre signed a fresh long-term contract at Wolves shortly after the Premier League season finished.

Clearly, he has bought into what the club is about, and he was obviously sold on the long-term project at Molineux.

The new contract was an initial four-year agreement, with Wolves having an option to extend it by another 12 months.

Of course, that doesn’t mean Andre can’t be sold, but many would’ve had the 13-cap Brazil international to be one of the certainties to leave after relegation.

So, the fact he didn’t push for a move back then, and actually committed his future to the club, suggests he is happy to stick around for at least one year.

With Wolves in a position to push for the top two, it’s unlikely that Andre’s situation will have changed too much at the moment, and his focus will be on helping the club back to the Premier League.

Looking beyond that, it seems inevitable that Andre will leave Wolves if they don’t win promotion this season.

Obviously, he won’t want another year in the Championship, and the club would be in a different financial position if they don’t go up, and Andre is undoubtedly a prized asset.

Sources indicate that will Wolves win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

But, that is a discussion for the summer, and all connected to Wolves will hope that Peixoto’s demands are met, which means Andre will see the season out.

If he does, and he maintains the levels he has set in the opening months, then there’s every chance Wolves will be celebrating promotion come May, and the midfielder will have made himself a hero at Molineux after showing remarkable loyalty following relegation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting CP in January 2020.

Bruno Fernandes has scored 113 goals in 341 appearances for Manchester United and has regularly carried the creative responsibility in midfield for the Red Devils.

His performances have remained amazing despite United struggling in recent times. Despite a sluggish start to the last season, Bruno Fernandes went on to register 21 Premier League assists, breaking the league’s single-season record.

Mauricio Pochettino will now have the opportunity to speak directly with the midfielder and make his own case for him to remain part of the project.

However, there are several complications still to resolve. The financial terms, length of the proposed contract and release clause will all need to be discussed before an agreement can be reached with the Portuguese midfielder.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to hold talks with Bruno Fernandes over his Manchester United future, with the club captain yet to agree a newly introduced contract at Old Trafford.

According to Fabrizio Romano, the new United head coach will now become involved in discussions with the Portuguese midfielder, whose current deal expires at the end of the season. The club have the option to extend it by a further 12 months, but are also keen to secure a longer-term agreement.

Manchester United have already held negotiations with Fernandes, but the 32-year-old has rejected two contract offers. Romano explained that Pochettino’s involvement could be an notable part of the talks, although the final decision will rest with Bruno Fernandes and United.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano stated: “First point: Mauricio Pochettino will be involved now in discussions with Bruno Fernandes.

“So, Pochettino will talk to Bruno, and he’s going to enter into this conversation.

“Then it’s going to be on Bruno, it’s going to be on the club.

“It’s a financial point, length of the contract, the release clause.

“It’s not Pochettino deciding yes or not, but Pochettino will be another factor now in the conversation.

“Then it’s on Bruno to decide.”.

According to recent reports, fernandes’ future is not settled at Manchester United and with Pochettino arriving at the club, he may have a different thought about his contract situation. Although a deal is not finalized yet but the talks will give the new head coach a chance to understand Fernandes’ position. However, the final call remains with Bruno Fernandes.

How can Mauricio Pochettino help Manchester United players to perform again?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to rediscover their winning mentality after agreeing to become the club’s upcoming head coach.
  • Manchester United announced Pochettino’s appointment just over 24 hours after confirming the departure of Michael Carrick.
  • In a recent development, he takes charge of United who sit in an embarrassing 18th place in the Premier League table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to rediscover their winning mentality after agreeing to become the club’s upcoming head coach.

Manchester United announced Pochettino’s appointment just over 24 hours after confirming the departure of Michael Carrick. The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager is believed to have agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford.

In a recent development, he takes charge of United who sit in an embarrassing 18th place in the Premier League table. They have managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, coming against Ipswich Town.

There is little time for the upcoming head coach to settle in, with a difficult first fixture against fierce rivals, Liverpool already awaiting him.

Speaking to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino made it clear that restoring confidence in the team and improving performances will be his immediate priorities.

“The most important thing for now is to start to work hard to recover that feeling about being a winner – to win games, to perform.”.

The Argentine hinted at sticking with the current crop of players to help them rediscover their form.

According to recent reports, “We need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players, we need to provide all the tools for them to perform.”.

Pochettino’s first match in charge will be one of the toughest possible introductions to English football’s biggest rivalry. Manchester United travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, giving Pochettino very little time to work with his squad before his first outing.

The new head coach faces a mountain ahead of him. He has walked into one of the most difficult jobs in world football. United have struggled so far into the season and they need results quickly to get them out of the relegation spots.

Pochettino has spoken about bringing back the winning feeling at Old Trafford, but his first challenge will be getting a response from his players who have managed only one league win in 10 games so far. That is far from Manchester United standards and Pochettino will be hoping he can instill some confidence back in the team.

The Liverpool game will offer an early indication of how his players respond to the change at United. A positive result would provide immediate relief for the under pressure United but the longer-term job of rebuilding United will take much more than one match.

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Top 7 best value-for-money EFL League One signings this season

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • League One clubs are always looking for value-for-money signings.
  • The majority of clubs in the third tier don't have millions and millions to throw around, so smart additions that can either be flipped for big profits in the future, or even those you bring in to perform one role and who can perform it perfectly, go a long way toward achieving success in the division.
  • This list won't just run down the best signings in League One so far this season, but instead look at those who have made such a massive impact that you can't help but feel the selling side should be given a little more money in retrospect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

League One clubs are always looking for value-for-money signings.

The majority of clubs in the third tier don't have millions and millions to throw around, so smart additions that can either be flipped for big profits in the future, or even those you bring in to perform one role and who can perform it perfectly, go a long way toward achieving success in the division.

This list won't just run down the best signings in League One so far this season, but instead look at those who have made such a massive impact that you can't help but feel the selling side should be given a little more money in retrospect.

Here are the seven best 'value for money' signings in League One this season.

A 32-year-old Jayden Stockley moving from Port Vale after their relegation to AFC Wimbledon isn't going to grab headlines at the time, but for a Dons side who know their backs are against the wall and will be forced to play direct, the frontman has been perfect for them.

Sources indicate that stockley reunited with ex-Charlton Athletic boss Johnnie Jackson in the summer, and was handed one role: win aerial duels and get us up the field. Now 33, the target man has been brilliant.

Recent findings suggest that he's been involved in 220 aerial duels, 81 more than anyone else in the division. The 112 he's won is 27 more than Paudie O'Connor in second place.

Plus, he's scored six league goals, which amounts to 60% of his side's total output. He's one of the main reasons why AFC Wimbledon are right now above the drop zone, and if they stay there, he'll be a key part of why, too.

Wigan Athletic had a substantial task on their hands this past summer in replacing academy graduate Sam Tickle after the goalkeeper made his well-deserved step-up to the Championship with Bristol City.

It seemed inevitable that the man to do so would be Joe Whitworth, whom Tics boss Gary Caldwell had loaned twice while at Exeter City from Crystal Palace, and they did so in a rather interesting deal.

The 22-year-old joined on a free transfer, with Palace holding a sell-on fee, meaning that Wigan will only have to pay the Premier League side a share of a future deal, rather than part ways with money now.

So far this season, Whitworth has prevented the most goals in the division, saved shots at a 70.2% rate and kept three clean sheets in 12 games, while also having above-average distribution numbers.

He's rapidly establishing himself as one of the best in his position, and for a free transfer, that's not bad at all.

It'll be mentioned a little later on in this list, but the ability to bring in someone who had such a great loan spell the season prior on a permanent deal for a cut-price, or in this case, for free, is incredible business.

Jon Russell has been revived under Nigel Clough at Mansfield Town after a strangely poor half-year at Barnsley under Conor Hourihane, after he netted 11 in 2024/25. He spent the latter half of last year at Field Mill, scoring five and assisting one in 21 league games.

The 26-year-old made his move permanent for free and has five goals and three assists in 13 games in all competitions so far this year for the Stags. He's been one of the best goalscoring midfielders in the division, and Clough seems to be playing to his strengths.

Mansfield continue to upset the odds and break newly introduced ceilings, and it's deals like this which help them do so.

According to recent reports, bradford City were among the best defensive sides in League One last season. Only four teams conceded fewer goals. They arguably didn't need to replace Sam Walker in goal, but if the right deal was there, Bantams fans were open to the idea.

In a recent development, in came Jon McCracken from Dundee FC on a free transfer, who had recorded the most saves and prevented 7.53 goals in the SPL last season. He was even linked with Celtic back in April. So, getting him for nothing was already a good start.

In a recent development, in his first 17 games as a Bantam, the Scotsman has registered 12 clean sheets, including nine in 12 league outings. Before shipping three against Huddersfield Town, he'd conceded just four goals in 11 games.

Sources indicate that that's quite exceptional, and the only thing perhaps limiting the amount of praise he should rightly get is the fact that Bradford as a whole are so great defensively. McCracken has only had to make 19 league saves all season, but he's still pulling through when called into action.

Derensili Sanches Fernandes has been the best player in League One this season. The man coined the 'dribble king' in the Dutch top flight at Excelsior has, unsurprisingly, been electric going forward against third-tier opposition, and has 13 goal involvements in 14 games.

According to recent reports, those involvements are as evenly split as you can imagine, too, with seven goals and six assists. Not only is he a great finisher, but he sets up chances better than anyone else, too. Indeed, no player has created more chances, nor big chances, than the 25-year-old.

He's even been capped by Cape Verde for the first time due to the quality he has shown at the Accu Stadium, and scored on his debut against Liberia in AFCON qualifiers.

But as good as Sanches Fernandes has been, he wasn't exactly cheap. Reports state that he moved to Huddersfield from Excelsior for "a significant" undisclosed fee, which could indicate a seven-figure sum. From that point of view, there are better value-for-money signings this season.

For the impact the wideman has made at his new club, though, Town fans feel like they may want to send the Dutch side a little more.

Luton Town's upturn in form towards the end of the season last year was not only down to Jack Wilshere becoming more settled in the dugout, but also due to the brilliance of Kasey Palmer, who joined on loan from Hull City.

In a recent development, in their 11-game unbeaten run to end the campaign, Palmer netted eight and assisted once. He also started in their EFL Trophy final win at Wembley against Stockport County. The Jamaican international had never played below the Championship before in his career, and was showcasing why.

It was imperative that Palmer made a permanent move if Luton were to continue their momentum from the latter stages of the previous year and go at least one place better than their seventh-place finish, and they managed to secure his services for less than £500,000.

For an attacking midfielder in his prime years, whose level is above League One, that's a brilliant bit of business, and he already has three goals and four assists in 12 league starts this season.

If he could help Jack Wilshere's side get back into the second-tier, it would be money well spent.

In terms of signing someone with big potential to be worth a lot more than the six-figure sum they initially paid, and who could help their side in the meantime push for promotion, no one comes close to Kyreece Lisbie.

Reports over the summer before a deal was made between Reading and Colchester United suggested that a fee between £500,000 and £750,000 would be needed, as Lisbie entered the final year of his deal at the League Two side, and already, he has the potential to be worth a decent seven-figure sum come the end of the campaign.

Who do you think has been the best value for money signing in League One so far this season? Let us know in the comments.

The pacy wideman has five goals and five assists in 15 games so far this season for Leam Richardson's side, profiting from the prolific nature of Jack Marriott but also getting into good goalscoring positions himself to help the Royals stay in and around the top six.

His twin brother, Kyrell, was sold to Millwall for between £2.5m and £3m this past summer after scoring 11 and assisting seven for Peterborough United. Kyreece is already over halfway to that goal-contribution tally and is performing for a side higher up in the division.

If he can keep this up, not only could he help Reading reach the second tier, but he could also bank the Royals a healthy profit immediately. Evidently, he has been the best value-for-money signing in League One so far.

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

📅 13 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 31 min read (6140 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~31 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • Recent findings suggest that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

Recent findings suggest that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent substantial players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

According to recent reports, the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Sources indicate that afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Sources indicate that maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a substantial team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

Sources indicate that the former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

It has been revealed that there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

According to recent reports, and the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

According to recent reports, patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the glitch then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

In a recent development, I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

Recent findings suggest that the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but major moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the initiative of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

Recent findings suggest that [On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

According to recent reports, changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

Sources indicate that it just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

It has been revealed that every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

It has been revealed that haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that indicates personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

“We had to change the blueprint a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

Industry observers note that and on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the substantial goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Sources indicate that dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

Recent findings suggest that united have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Sources indicate that good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

It has been revealed that nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Industry observers note that fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

According to recent reports, it’s a massive final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

It has been revealed that united were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

“You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

It has been revealed that both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

In a recent development, rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very crucial in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

Recent findings suggest that with Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.
