  • The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

Industry observers note that around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel. The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his latest squad, but its release promptly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its upcoming head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

It has been revealed that “Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”.

Manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a big reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in key matches.

“A recurring concern with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of substantial trophies.”.

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in big games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

“Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

Sources indicate that the Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

Norwich City have won five games on the spin following their 2-1 home victory over Cardiff City at the weekend, and one player's upturn in form has coincided with this incredible streak.

Norwich's campaign thus far has been something of a rollercoaster, as, after 16 games, the Canaries are still yet to draw a game in the Championship this season, winning eight and losing eight.

According to recent reports, now on a five-game unbeaten run courtesy of victories over Charlton Athletic, Watford, Derby County, Bristol City, and Cardiff, Norwich have flown up the table. However, before this winning run came to fruition, a six-game losing streak across all competitions preceded it.

Belgian head coach Philippe Clement will certainly be hoping for more consistency moving forward, and with the January window approaching, may well also be looking to replicate some past transfers.

With Clement arriving at Carrow Road in November 2025, the former Monaco and Rangers boss has officially ticked over a year in charge in Norfolk, and it would be fair to suggest there have been more highs than lows during his reign.

The January 2026 window proved to be especially fruitful for the 52-year-old, who oversaw the additions of the likes of Sam Field, Ali Ahmed, Mohamed Toure, and Paris Maghoma at Norwich.

Maghoma, 25, joined from Premier League outfit Brentford in a deal worth around £800k, having worked his way up the EFL with loans at AFC Wimbledon, Milton Keynes Dons, and Bolton Wanderers, but failing to nail down a place in the Bees' side.

The former Tottenham Hotspur youth prospect scored once and grabbed three assists in 14 Championship games during his first six months at the club, but now has seemingly found his groove.

At the beginning of this campaign, Maghoma initially struggled to nail down a place in the Norwich starting XI, as after playing 71 minutes in the 2-1 home defeat to West Bromwich Albion in the season opener, the Englishman would have to wait nearly another month for his next league appearance.

He grabbed assists in defeats to Middlesbrough and Bolton, and after six defeats on the spin, Maghoma was finally introduced back into the starting lineup away to Charlton, grabbing the equaliser in a 3-1 victory.

Since then, the attacking midfielder has surpassed Anis Ben Slimane and Oscar Schwartau to a place in Clement's first XI, and with four goals in four games following his strike against Charlton, has duly rewarded the Belgian for his faith.

The attacking midfielder has found his stride in the Championship, and if he can continue this level of form, Norwich will certainly feel as though they have struck the transfer jackpot.

Having signed Maghoma for just £800k, Norwich will already be rubbing their hands at the prospect of a potential lucrative sale in the near future, especially if he can continue this rich vein of form.

The Englishman never managed to make a senior appearance during his time at Spurs, and with just ten first-team appearances for Brentford, his potential was never realised or displayed in West London.

Now, Norwich are reaping the rewards for taking the gamble and putting faith in Maghoma, as he could well help guide the Canaries back to the Premier League, or, at the very least, reward them with an enormous profit.

According to recent reports, what have you made of Paris Maghoma's recent form for Norwich City? How much is he realistically worth now? Will Spurs and Brentford be feeling any transfer envy? Share your thoughts below!

With Toure and Ahmed out injured as of late, Clement has had to look elsewhere in his squad for somebody to take the mantle and become the main attacking threat in the side, and that appears to be Maghoma.

Mathias Kvistgaarden, Anthony Musaba, Andre Brooks, and Jovon Makama have each played their parts too, but it is the attacking midfielder who has drawn headlines for his performances and displays.

If Norwich are to achieve anything special this season, then Maghoma will surely be at the forefront of that success, as Spurs and Brentford may be feeling some transfer envy right now.

Gerry Cardinale had a meeting with the AC Milan management at Casa Milan yesterday, during which there were four key topics, according to reports.

There could be a lot of substantial movement in the coming months, in other words, as Cardinale is really pushing for these things to materialise. Of course, other matters were also discussed during the meeting but as Longo highlighted, those mentioned above were the main ones.

Mauricio Pochettino has made it clear he wants to be involved in Manchester United’s major squad decisions, while also addressing questions surrounding captain Bruno Fernandes ahead of his first game against Liverpool.

The new Manchester United head coach explained that he wants to have a voice in decisions that shape the squad.

“Sometimes maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions,” Pochettino stated in his first Manchester United press conference.

“It depends on the structure, it depends on the communication, the relationships, you know, with all the areas.”.

Mauricio Pochettino highlighted his responsibilities are clear about who he selects and plays in games.].

“I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I’m going to pick the team, I’m going to make the changes, and of course in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad.”.

Pochettino was also asked about Bruno Fernandes, whose critical comments about Michael Carrick’s tactics became a talking point during the former manager’s final weeks at Old Trafford.

The Argentine was really keen about the squad’s commitment, dodging the blame on Fernandes and describing Fernandes as a key figure in the dressing room.

“The commitment from all the players was amazing from day one,” he stated.

“Bruno is our captain and a very key player but all the players need to feel they are important from the bottom to the top.”.

Pochettino revealed that he had already spent time speaking with the players to understand their situation both on and off the pitch.

“Yesterday we spent three hours chatting to the players in my office and maybe I missed the injured players.”.

Pochettino admitted the first few days at United had been extremely busy as he tried to get up to speed before his first match.

He is excited by the opportunity but knows there is little time to prepare for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

“It’s a happy time but at the same time, so busy,” he explained.

“It’s been about adapting in the last few days, and it’s a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool in the game on Sunday.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Fernandes has been at the center of contract talks this season and is yet to sign a new deal at Manchester United.
  • In a recent development, various reports have indicated that Bruno Fernandes has turned down two contract offers.
  • Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has confirmed the club are discussing a new contract with Bruno Fernandes, but has refused to reveal any details about the negotiations as the midfielder approaches the final months of his current deal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes has been at the center of contract talks this season and is yet to sign a new deal at Manchester United.

In a recent development, various reports have indicated that Bruno Fernandes has turned down two contract offers. He reportedly wants a 4-year deal but United are wary of such a deal as he is already 32 years old.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has confirmed the club are discussing a new contract with Bruno Fernandes, but has refused to reveal any details about the negotiations as the midfielder approaches the final months of his current deal.

Fernandes’ contract expires at the end of the season, leaving Manchester United with an important decision to make over the future of their captain.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Berrada praised the Portuguese international for his contribution to the club and made clear how highly he is valued at Old Trafford.

“Listen, I’ve stated before, we have a tremendous amount of respect for Bruno,” Berrada said.

“We’re very fortunate to have him as a captain.

“What he’s done for this team over the last six, seven years is absolutely incredible. Last year he won, I think, all the individual awards that you can win.

Industry observers note that “And we’re very proud to have him as captain. It’s true that we’re having conversations about his latest contract, but I prefer to keep that private.

“I think it’s something that needs to be discussed behind the scenes between him and the club.”.

Sources indicate that although contract talks are taking place, there is no indication of how close the two parties are to reaching an agreement. United will be keen to avoid losing one of their most influential players throughout these years, but the terms and length of any new contract remain speculative at the moment.

Latest manager, Mauricio Pochettino, has backed his captain ahead of his first game against Liverpool. He was asked about Bruno Fernandes, whose critical comments about Michael Carrick’s tactics became a talking point during the former manager’s final weeks at Old Trafford.

The newly introduced head coach did not get drawn into the controversy, instead stressing the importance of Fernandes to the team and the need for every player to feel valued.

“Bruno is our captain and a very important player but all the players need to feel they are important from the bottom to the top,” Pochettino said.

It has been revealed that the Bruno Fernandes contract situation comes at a difficult time for United, who are 18th in the Premier League with eight points from their opening 10 matches. They have managed just one win and five draws during that run.

Pochettino has inherited a struggling side, and keeping Bruno Fernandes committed to the project could prove notable as he is one of the few performing stars in the fragile Manchester United team.

One Chris Davies quality at Birmingham City is 'beyond anything' Tom Huddlestone has seen

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Birmingham City assistant coach and former Premier League midfielder, Tom Huddlestone, has issued a stunning claim on the coaching level of current St.
  • Davies is now in his third season in charge of Blues, having taken over in June 2024 ahead of the club's solitary League One campaign this century.
  • His tenure hasn't been without mixed reviews, but right now the West Midlands outfit are fourth in the Championship, having lost for just a third time this campaign on Saturday against Stoke City in underwhelming fashion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City assistant coach and former Premier League midfielder, Tom Huddlestone, has issued a stunning claim on the coaching level of current St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park boss, Chris Davies.

Davies is now in his third season in charge of Blues, having taken over in June 2024 ahead of the club's solitary League One campaign this century.

His tenure hasn't been without mixed reviews, but right now the West Midlands outfit are fourth in the Championship, having lost for just a third time this campaign on Saturday against Stoke City in underwhelming fashion.

Davies' side will be hoping for a swift response when they face lowly Burnley on Wednesday night, with it representing another chance for the 41-year-old to show why he is so highly thought of.

Davies oversaw the most remarkable first season at St. Andrew's, with his side breaking the EFL's all-time points record en route back to the Championship, before finishing 10th last term.

There were some question marks over his future following a 6-1 EFL Cup loss to Brentford in August, but aside from three away losses to Norwich City, Cardiff City and Stoke, Birmingham have looked largely impressive across all departments.

Huddlestone, 39, became one of Davies' assistants in September 2024 after a brief spell at Wigan Athletic with former Hull City teammate, Shaun Maloney.

Asked how the game has changed from a coaching perspective by another ex-Hull colleague, Aaron McLean, and Adam Virgo, the former England international heaped praise on both head coaches.

"The detail that Shaun and Chris go into is beyond anything I've seen in terms of every little detail," Huddlestone revealed.

"Full clarity on how we press, how we play.

"A lot of stuff in my career, before Marco Silva (at Hull), was generally quite off-the-cuff, to be honest," he added.

"You'd have a system, know which three or four players you wanted to get the ball, but other than that, it was like 'go and do your thing'.

"The clarity is the biggest thing, and the details, even in throw-ins and every little detail in the game is nailed down and gone through.".

There has certainly been shifts in how Birmingham have played in the early weeks of the current season compared to last, with an onus on moving the ball at speed and being direct when required.

Blues averaged 53.7% possession in last season's Championship, which was the seventh-highest total, but now have the ball just 51.6% of the time inside the first 16 matches.

Although there isn't much of a difference between such numbers, the way in which Birmingham have attacked has required far less time on the ball due to the speed of forwards such as Liam Millar and Patrick Roberts, as well as the intelligence of August Priske and Jay Stansfield.

Davies also admitted pre-season that more goals were required in order to sustain a promotion bid, and such feats have certainly been the case, whilst 15 concessions mean Blues have the joint-best defensive record along with Southampton.

Huddlestone played 242 times at Premier League level under some of the game's most experienced figures, such as Steve Bruce, Harry Redknapp and Glenn Hoddle.

The former technically gifted midfielder also knows what it takes to earn promotion from the Championship, having done so with Hull 10 years ago, and such knowledge will be pivotal for Davies and Birmingham's current squad to lean on.

Blues fans, can Chris Davies become an elite-level manager? Comment below!

Huddlestone is also right now coaching with Ben Futcher as part of the England Under-20s setup, and it may not be too long until we see him lead a team in the dugout, having recently stated: “I do want to try my hand at managing, but I’m not in no rush for that.".

Latest Update: Barnsley relegation problem identified as January transfer demand emerges

💡 Key Takeaways
  • EFL content creator and Barnsley fan Callum Fowler believes that Barnsley are a striker away from climbing out of the bottom four in League One.
  • The Tykes' winless league run reached 10 games on Friday night at Oakwell against Sheffield Wednesday, as the Owls were clinical when needed, scoring twice in the opening 14 minutes and keeping the hosts at arm's length thereafter.
  • In a recent development, but it was another game in which Daniel Stendel's side outshot their opponents and had more touches in their box, and that's been the story of their season so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EFL content creator and Barnsley fan Callum Fowler believes that Barnsley are a striker away from climbing out of the bottom four in League One.

The Tykes' winless league run reached 10 games on Friday night at Oakwell against Sheffield Wednesday, as the Owls were clinical when needed, scoring twice in the opening 14 minutes and keeping the hosts at arm's length thereafter.

In a recent development, but it was another game in which Daniel Stendel's side outshot their opponents and had more touches in their box, and that's been the story of their season so far. Barnsley are poor in both boxes, hence their position at the foot of the League One table.

January is going to be crucial if the Reds are going to avoid a first fourth-tier campaign since the late 1970s, and a striker must be atop their shopping list.

Speaking on the weekly Pyramid podcast, EFL content creator and Barnsley supporter Callum Fowler admitted that he doesn't feel his side are playing badly, and that a striker is all that separates them from being adrift at the bottom of the third tier and mid-table.

The Reds have relied heavily on goals from the midfield so far this season. In all competitions, Cameron McGeehan is their top scorer with nine, closely followed by Vimal Yoganathan, who has eight, and Reyes Cleary is below on six.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Portsmouth loanee Makenzie Kirk sits on four in all competitions, and just two in League One action. The Tykes fan ran through the squad and admitted, especially in midfield, that they're not a bad side, but don't have that focal point leading the line.

It has been revealed that "When our nines are worse than me and you, and our depth is non-existent. The striker…imagine you replace your most notable player with me up front; we don’t have a striker," he remarked.

"I look at the scores coming in, and Wycombe have scored, and every time it’s [Jayden] Wareham. If we just had someone like him up front...every team has a better striker than we do, 100%.".

Fowler is almost resigned to Cleary leaving the club in the upcoming January transfer window, as the higher-ups look to maximise his value in case they do fall into League Two in the summer, and he hopes that they use whatever money they get from the deal to buy a recognised striker.

"It's got to be a thing in January; we know Cleary’s going to go, five million, whatever, if they do not spend that money..." he continued.

Recent findings suggest that "They [Sheffield Wednesday] were better than us for 15 minutes; they had two shots all game. I’m saying, I know we’re bottom, but seriously, if we had a striker with legs we’d be about 14th, 13th.".

In a recent development, this time last year, Barnsley were lining up with Davis Keillor-Dunn and David McGoldrick as their strikers. In less than 12 months, Tykes fans can't believe how they've been downgraded.

Recent findings suggest that this past summer, the only striker who was bought at Oakwell was Ben Hamed Toure, whose time in South Yorkshire has yet to get going due to a devastating family bereavement. Maybe he can hit the ground running now he's back, but Barnsley fans aren't holding their breath.

It has been revealed that the fact that they've had to resort to two free agents since the summer window closed is pretty telling in itself. But in Tobi Adeyemo, who scored one goal in League Two last season for a poor Crawley Town side, and Rylan Brownlie, who, in fairness, has looked lively, they've continued to sign unproven youngsters.

Sources indicate that who do you think Barnsley should sign in the January transfer window? Let us know in the comments.

Industry observers note that and they've been made to pay the price. Barnsley's attacking numbers indicate they'd be one of the best sides going forward in the division. Per Opta, they've taken the sixth-most shots, the 11th most on target, and have the seventh most touches in the opposition's box.

In reality, only AFC Wimbledon, Bradford City, Notts County and Peterborough United have scored fewer.

Sheffield Wednesday showed that you don't have to do much to beat Barnsley. Their two goals were incredibly easy to score, and while the Tykes controlled the game after that, they didn't do much to trouble the Owls' backline.

According to recent reports, wigan Athletic boss Gary Caldwell admitted after their 2-1 win over the Reds that he was happy to let Daniel Stendel's side have the ball and come onto them, as they often lose games when that's the case. In league games where Barnsley have had over 55% of the ball, their record is P8, W1, D1, L6.

And, ultimately, if Barnsley had that potent goalscorer leading the line, games in which they have the ball would see them punish sides much more often, and Daniel Stendel's playstyle, which isn't bad, would get much more out of this set of players.

Strikers are the ones who cost the significant bucks, and while Neerav Parekh and co haven't been the best spenders in recent years, they need to pull out all the stops if their side is to remain in this division this season.

  • According to recent reports, manchester United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, with one win and five draws leaving them 18th in the table.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino begins his Manchester United reign with a huge test at Anfield on Sunday, with Manchester United desperate for a result after making their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.

According to recent reports, manchester United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, with one win and five draws leaving them 18th in the table. They have also conceded in every league game this season and are right now on a run of 11 consecutive matches without keeping a clean sheet in all competitions.

Mauricio Pochettino only arrived to the club on Wednesday after replacing Michael Carrick, leaving him with just a few training sessions to prepare for one of the biggest fixtures in English football.

There is some encouragement for the Argentine, however. Eight of United’s last nine permanent or caretaker managers have avoided defeat in their first match in charge. That may be some encouragement to the Argentine.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Liverpool are not exactly enjoying a comfortable season at home either. They sit fourth with 18 points but have won just once in their five Premier League matches at Anfield so far, giving them the third-worst home record in the Premier League.

Their recent form across all competitions stands at three wins, one draw and two defeats in their last six matches. Liverpool most recently beat Crystal Palace 3-1, but they will know that United’s poor league position does not make this fixture any less complicated.

Sources indicate that liverpool have received positive news ahead of Sunday’s meeting. Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk are both expected to feature, while Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong could also be available.

Recent findings suggest that conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to team training following knee injuries but are unlikely to make the squad. Hugo Ekitike remains a long-term absentee with an Achilles problem.

Manchester United could welcome back Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire after both trained following fitness concerns. They were seen in that leaked drone footage as well. Lisandro Martínez is also available again after serving his suspension.

Sources indicate that luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford could return, although their availability remains uncertain. Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are still sidelined.

Recent findings suggest that the newly introduced United boss has a difficult personal record against Liverpool. Pochettino has faced the Reds 19 times, winning three, drawing five and losing 11. He has also failed to win any of his last eight meetings with them in all competitions. That might be a concern, but everything has a first time.

Pochettino will be encouraged by United’s overall record against Liverpool. United have an edge with 85 wins compared to Liverpool’s 72 across 218 meetings. Their most recent encounter also went their way, with a 3-2 victory on May 3.

However, United arrive on a disappointing run of seven consecutive away matches without a win and have managed just one victory in their last 11 games.

West Ham & Middlesbrough sent warning over what Wolves are doing right now

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham and Middlesbrough have been warned that Wolves have the potential to win the Championship if they ‘click into gear’.
  • It has been a positive start to life at Molineux for Cesar Peixoto, with his side sitting third and just one point away from league leaders Boro going into the midweek set of fixtures, where Wanderers host lowly Derby.
  • Yet, despite the good position, Wolves fans haven’t been totally convinced by Peixoto or the team, with chants directed against the manager as recently as last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham and Middlesbrough have been warned that Wolves have the potential to win the Championship if they ‘click into gear’.

It has been a positive start to life at Molineux for Cesar Peixoto, with his side sitting third and just one point away from league leaders Boro going into the midweek set of fixtures, where Wanderers host lowly Derby.

Yet, despite the good position, Wolves fans haven’t been totally convinced by Peixoto or the team, with chants directed against the manager as recently as last month.

Even if Wolves haven’t always impressed with their performances, they have found a way of getting results, and they head into the Derby game unbeaten in seven, picking up 17 points in that period.

The latest victory was a 2-1 success over Charlton, which was much more comfortable than the scoreline suggests, as Peixoto’s side were rarely troubled all afternoon.

So, they are building momentum, and speaking on The Pyramid Podcast, Jimmy from the Blades Ramble explained how Wolves have gone under the radar somewhat, as he stated they could still have more to offer, which makes them a huge threat in the title race.

“Wolves are just getting it done. Even when they haven’t been turning up (performances), they’ve been doing enough. So, it worries me that if they turn it on, and click into gear, and reach another level, they could be the ones.

“This is the opportunity for Wolves though, because everyone said West Ham, but Wolves aren’t that far behind West Ham (in terms of quality), but they’ve been overlooked because of West Ham being in the league. It shouldn’t surprise anyone if Wolves go on and win this league (even if) I still think Middlesbrough are the team to beat.”.

There’s no denying that Wolves haven’t been a free-flowing, exciting team to watch for large parts this season, but it should be stated that they are very solid defensively, which gives you a good foundation to pick up points.

Peixoto walked into a club in a very difficult situation, as the fans are understandably furious with the owners for their rapid decline in recent years, and that anger is still there.

Plus, there is a feeling that more promises were broken in the summer because of the way the window played out, which has made it difficult for the supporters to fully embrace Peixoto and the team.

But, to his credit, Peixoto has navigated through that very well in terms of results, and if Wolves can beat Derby, they will be on two points a game after 17, which is a brilliant return.

Many would agree that there should still be more to come from this Wolves side, as whilst they are good defensively, the attacking players haven’t hit the heights many expected.

Mateus Mane and Rodrigo Gomes aren’t showing their best levels consistently, whilst Adam Armstrong is only just scoring regularly after a slow start. Meanwhile, Fer Lopez’s influence on the team has reduced, even if he remains a superb talent, and Jordan James hasn’t really got going in Old Gold.

When you add in that Raul Jimenez has missed most of the season through injury and won’t return until January, it just highlights why people think Wolves are capable of doing so much more.

Will Wolves win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

And, that should worry their promotion rivals, because if those attacking players do find their best form, Wolves, on paper, have a team that is capable of putting winning runs together.

So, the challenge for Peixoto and the players is to make that happen, as Wolves do have the talent and squad depth to go all the way this season.

#164170. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5394 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5394 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half.
  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

Sources indicate that it has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

In a recent development, the home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a substantial evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

According to recent reports, big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Industry observers note that leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

According to recent reports, jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

Industry observers note that A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

Sources indicate that “That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

It has been revealed that [It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

Recent findings suggest that it’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

It has been revealed that exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

According to recent reports, for each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Recent findings suggest that energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

It has been revealed that we have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

In a recent development, I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I mentioned to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

According to recent reports, it’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

Industry observers note that it’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

According to recent reports, james pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Industry observers note that late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

It has been revealed that leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Livramento drives the ball 60 yards looking for Barnes but the ball skids off the turf and into Trafford’s arms.

Crunching Bard tackle on Bamba sends the ball to James who lets fly from 22 yards into the shins of a Newcastle defender.

Bard is penalised for a trip on Barnes as the game peters out.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Sources indicate that jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the upcoming boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. Why can Mauricio Pochettino turn things around at Manchester United?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United have struggled badly this season, sitting 18th in the Premier League after collecting just eight points from their opening 10 matches.
  • Sources indicate that pochettino replaces Michael Carrick and his job has been described as one of the toughest jobs in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first United game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with plenty of questions surrounding the players who will benefit from his arrival.

Manchester United have struggled badly this season, sitting 18th in the Premier League after collecting just eight points from their opening 10 matches.

Sources indicate that pochettino replaces Michael Carrick and his job has been described as one of the toughest jobs in the Premier League. Former defender Wes Brown believes Manchester United have a chance with Pochettino to change things despite it being very difficult.

Brown believes the new manager has enough quality at his disposal to improve the situation, despite the difficult start and the pressure that comes with the Manchester United job.

Asked whether Pochettino faces an impossible task after previous managers failed to bring success to Old Trafford, Brown was confident the Argentine could make a difference.

“Definitely not impossible. Regardless of what has happened so far this season, Manchester United do have good players,” Wes Brown noted while talking to Flashscore.

Brown expects Pochettino to demand more effort from the squad.

“He looks like a personable manager, so can work with these players individually to get their confidence up and really play for the shirt and create that positive vibe that seems to be missing.”.

Asked about how long Manchester United will take to be a title challenger again, Wes Brown was cautious in putting any numbers.

“Well, it isn’t going to happen overnight. You will need a reaction swiftly, that is for sure. They are very far away, but you have to start with consistency and that is something Pochettino has to install and deliver a consistency of play, to be fitter than your opponent and show fight.”.

The former defender also highlighted Bruno Fernandes’ drop in form, suggesting the captain could benefit from a change in management.

“You have to see Bruno’s form has dropped, so it will be great to see this pick up under the upcoming manager.”.

Pochettino’s priority will be getting a response on Sunday against Liverpool from his senior players. United have been in this cycle of repeating managers and not finding much success. Mauricio Pochettino needs to take things one at a time. Sunday would be that first step.

Chelsea’s wide-player search has moved back into focus after the Guardian reported that the club are monitoring West Ham pair Jarrod Bowen and Crysencio Summerville.

The update lands during a busy early market for Xabi Alonso’s incoming rebuild.

The Guardian’s latest transfer round-up states that Chelsea like both West Ham forwards, while an earlier report noted Chelsea and Manchester United had tracked Summerville.

That same earlier enhancement also said Aston Villa, Chelsea and Everton had expressed interest in Bowen.

Sources indicate that west Ham pulling away at Stamford Bridge 👀Jarrod Bowen stuns Chelsea early before Crysencio Summerville doubles the lead. pic.twitter.com/Ktwr4pKZGH.

Alonso officially begins work on July 1, with Chelsea confirming he has signed a four-year contract to lead the men’s team.

In a recent development, the winger search is not just about adding more attacking names. It is about identifying profiles who can quickly give Chelsea sharper final-third decisions.

Bowen would offer immediate Premier League output, penalty-box timing and a direct threat from the right.

Summerville, meanwhile, fits the younger, explosive one-v-one profile that would sit neatly inside Alonso’s longer-term wing plan.

Read Chelsea has already tracked the separate Summerville angle, but this latest dual link sharpens the picture.

Chelsea appear to be testing two different solutions to the same problem: proven reliability or higher-upside acceleration.

With pre-season closing in, that is exactly the sort of market check Alonso needs before deciding how much of Chelsea’s attacking rebuild should lean on speed, touchline width and more ruthless wide output.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.
  • Recent findings suggest that the figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.

United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.

Recent findings suggest that the figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis. That total is expected to rise once the costs of Michael Carrick’s dismissal and appointing Pochettino’s coaching staff are included.

Sources indicate that pochettino signed a two-and-a-half-year contract on 13 November, replacing Carrick after a difficult start to the Premier League season. The club’s Stock Market filing states that the appointment fee will be recognised in its financial accounts for the current quarter. United also confirmed borrowing a further £10m on 16 November, taking the amount drawn on their revolving credit facility to £240m.

Pochettino is United’s ninth full-time managerial appointment since Ferguson’s departure, including Ralf Rangnick’s interim spell. The club have also changed managers during each of the past three seasons.

It has been revealed that united’s financial disclosures show that their long-term debt stood at £577.4m on 30 September, while outstanding transfer-fee commitments totalled £417m. Those figures are separate from the cost of appointing and dismissing managers.

Sources indicate that A Reuters analysis has put the wider cost of managerial and senior football staff changes above £100m, using a broader calculation. Pochettino now faces the task of improving United’s results, beginning with Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City's hunt for an heir to Vitor Matos has now taken another twist, with the Welsh outfit having set their sights on former Iceland women's head coach Freyr Alexandersson.

Swansea were rocked by the news of the departure of former head coach Vitor Matos last week, with the former Liverpool and RB Salzburg coach choosing to head to France and link up with Chelsea-affiliated BlueCo outfit Strasbourg.

As a result, a coaching team consisting of Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, and Joe Allen have taken charge of things in Swansea for now as the hunt for Matos' replacement continues, as a surprise latest contender has emerged.

According to The Telegraph's Mike McGrath, Icelandic coach Freyr Alexandersson has emerged as the leading contender for the vacant role at the Swansea.com Stadium, having held talks with the club.

Alexandersson, 44, began his coaching career aged just 26, assisting Valur's women's team in his native Iceland, before spells with Leiknir Reykjavík, Iceland women's national team, Iceland men's national team, Al-Arabi, Lyngby, Kortrijk, SK Brann, and now Rosenborg followed.

Swansea have a partnership with Jamestown Analytics, the same model that Brighton and Hove Albion use to recruit players and staff, and that system has likely played a part in the sounding out of Alexandersson.

The current Rosenborg boss has his side sitting in 4th in the Norwegian Eliteserien as things stand, some 18 points behind league leader Bodo/Glimt, as Swansea are trusting their data with this potential appointment.

Unsurprisingly, Swansea were not entirely pleased with the swift departure of Matos, as with Strasbourg's interest emerging, a deal that saw the former Jürgen Klopp understudy head to France was done barely 48 hours later.

Swansea have received a compensation fee in excess of £5 million for Matos, though having been allowed to build the team in his image and get them flying towards the top of the league, it's not the end of the relationship either party surely would've hoped for.

In a statement released by Swansea, the club barely touched on Matos' exit, saying: "Per RC Strasbourg's announcement, Swansea City acknowledges that Vitor Matos and his coaching staff have left the club.".

Now, the hunt for a replacement continues, with Alexandersson emerging from nowhere to go into pole position for the role, as the Welsh outfit looks to maintain their push for promotion in a fresh era.

In a recent development, what do you make of this potential appointment? Who would you like to see replace Vitor Matos at Swansea? Share your thoughts below!

With Williams and a bunch of Swansea favourites over the years taking the helm for now, the club will hope they can remain in contention for automatic promotion moving forward after this jarring and unexpected period.

Whether Alexandersson will be the correct person to take the club forward remains to be seen, as Swansea are putting their faith in Jamestown Analytics and leaning into the data model fully for this potential appointment.

Time will tell how this one plays out, as Swansea fans won't care who is in charge as long as they can maintain their push towards the top of the Championship and forget all about Matos in due course.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a major responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really key because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”.

On those involved in international duty….

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”.

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

In a recent development, “Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

Industry observers note that “Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

Sources indicate that “They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I stated against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause concerns.”.

In a recent development, camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

It has been revealed that “Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

In a recent development, “It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”.

Sources indicate that are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

Industry observers note that “Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”.

During the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

Recent findings suggest that “I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That noted, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

It has been revealed that “I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini stated himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”.

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games….

Sources indicate that “Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

Industry observers note that “If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”.

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed….

Recent findings suggest that “That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

“Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”.

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really crucial for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how important he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

In a recent development, “I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”.

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

It has been revealed that “That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

Sources indicate that “Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your blueprint. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”.

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

It has been revealed that “I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”.

Is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

“I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

It has been revealed that this matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

According to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

That statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

In a recent development, data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Recent findings suggest that within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Recent findings suggest that prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

Industry observers note that for Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a big boost. It could help fund latest signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

It has been revealed that city chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

According to recent reports, chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

According to recent reports, the Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes has been Manchester United’s most creative player since his arrival to the club in 2020.

In a recent development, the 32-year-old is approaching the final months of his current deal, which expires at the end of the season. United do have the option to extend his contract by another 12 months, keeping him at Old Trafford until 2028.

While they can extend his contract for a year, Manchester United are actively pursuing a deal to tie Bruno Fernandes beyond 2028.

Bruno Fernandes himself has now confirmed that the club have offered him a fresh contract, but the midfielder has made it clear that he does not want discussions about his future to become a priority right now.

Fernandes confirmed that an offer had been made but dismissed suggestions that he was holding out for a better salary or a longer agreement.

“The club offered me a upcoming contract, so I think that, from their side, reveals that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

He also insisted that money has never been the reason behind his decision to remain at United, despite having opportunities to move elsewhere in previous transfer windows.

“If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here,” Fernandes said.

The Portugal international added that he could have earned considerably more by accepting offers from other clubs, but always chose to continue his career in Manchester.

Fernandes revealed that discussions initially took place towards the end of last season and continued when the players returned for pre-season.

However, the United captain believes the current situation at the club makes it the wrong time to focus on his personal future.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side,” he explained.

“I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”.

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting in 2020. He has scored 75 Premier League goals for the club and set a new competition record for assists in a single season last term.

Industry observers note that bruno’s comments don’t sound like he is holding United hostage demanding more pay or refusing to sign a fresh one. The intention as told by Bruno Fernandes just show his leadership trait about putting the team first. He has no immediate intention of making his contract situation the centre of attention. That will be a sign of encouragement for the fans as well.

Manchester United need to start winning games again. When they do and surely Bruno Fernandes will be at the centre of it, the contract talks can resume and take priority.

Ronnie Edwards was signed permanently from Southampton by Queens Park Rangers and has had particular praise from former QPR and Saints striker Charlie Austin.

Having played as both a defensive midfielder and a centre-back since his initial arrival on loan to Queens Park Rangers from Southampton, Edwards has since made one of the two central defensive positions his own this season.

Sources indicate that jimmy Dunne has also been excellent as his partner for the majority of games, but Jake Clarke-Salter is also a strong performer at Championship level when fit. Between them, they are an excellent combination of options for Julien Stephan.

It has been revealed that speaking via his show on The Charlie Austin Football Channel on YouTube, Austin talked up the 23-year-old and said: "Well, Ronnie Edwards at £4.5 million, come from Southampton. I mean, what a steal that is from Southampton.

It has been revealed that "Look, I played against him, Peter. I want to say, when I was at West Brom against Peterborough [United]. And I played against him, I thought, 'This young man, he's tidy. He's good him'. Then I played against QPR I think it was again.

"I always thought he would go on to bigger things other than Southampton, if I'm being honest without being rude. Or he would use that as a stepping stone and move on but he's gone to QPR.

"He went to QPR on loan, he had a great time there. I mean, listen, I don't think you change a winning team, but listen, I've had my frustrations with Julien at times because he hasn't kept certain players in the team when they performed the game previously.

"Like with [Rumarn] Burrell, we scored two won one game midweek and then he was dropped at the weekend. I couldn't get my head around it if I'm honest as a centre-forward.".

Edwards emerged at Peterborough, making his senior breakthrough as a teenager before establishing himself as one of League One's most exciting young centre-backs.

It has been revealed that his performances earned him a £3 million move to Southampton in 2024 (BBC Sport), having also helped England win the European Under-19 Championship. Edwards is an assured operator in possession, comfortable carrying the ball forward, and breaking lines.

In a recent development, he can find teammates between the lines by punching passes into forward areas, too. He is also proactive in defensive duels, although his aerial ability and tendency to be over-aggressive remain areas for improvement if he is to become a Premier League player.

In a recent development, now one of the Championship's outstanding defenders at QPR, Southampton may regret selling him for a reported £4.5 million initially (Daily Echo). Had they been a bit more patient, he could be their asset worth a lot more than he is now.

It has been revealed that austin is spot on with his praise of Edwards, who looks increasingly like the sort of defender Southampton should have been building their future around. Allowing a young, homegrown, English talent to slip through their fingers to QPR for so little will be particularly frustrating.

Southampton are understandably focused on securing promotion, and their recruitment reflects that, but sustainable clubs cannot afford to neglect player development, even in the midst of that.
