📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 12:11.

Arsenal could face a fresh complication in their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with Paris Saint-Germain reportedly considering whether to accelerate their interest in the Frenchman following Desire Doue's serious knee injury.

The European champions were already among the clubs monitoring Kroupi ahead of the January transfer window, but their attacking situation has become considerably more difficult after Doue was stretchered off during Saturday's 3-2 Ligue 1 victory over Nice. PSG confirmed on Sunday that the 21-year-old has ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will undergo surgery before the end of November.

According to TEAMtalk transfer correspondent Graeme Bailey, PSG hold a strong interest in the Bournemouth attacker, who is also wanted by Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur. The French champions could now consider stepping up their pursuit, although no formal approach or offer has been reported.

It has been revealed that any attempt to secure the youngster's signature would present a substantial financial challenge. Bournemouth are understood to value Kroupi at upwards of £80m and have shown little willingness to entertain a mid-season departure, despite increasing attention from some of Europe's leading clubs.

Doue's confirmed ACL rupture has left Luis Enrique facing a potentially season-ending absence in a forward line already weakened by the loss of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

The France international had scored PSG's second goal against Nice before suffering the injury late in the first half. He required treatment on the pitch and was eventually carried off on a stretcher, with Ferran Torres replacing him and subsequently scoring the winning goal.

Luis Enrique warned after the match that the injury was serious, although he stressed that further medical examinations were needed to establish its precise nature.

Those concerns were confirmed on Sunday when PSG announced that Doue had suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. The club also confirmed that the forward would undergo surgery before the end of November.

Although PSG have not declared a definitive recovery timetable, the severity of the injury raises serious doubts about whether Doue will play again this season.

The setback follows Kvaratskhelia's ACL injury during PSG's Champions League victory over Barcelona in October, which has already deprived Enrique of another notable attacking option.

Sources indicate that paris still possess considerable depth, with Ousmane Dembele, Torres, Manuel Akliouche and Mika Godts among the players available to the Spanish coach. Nevertheless, losing two influential attackers in relatively quick succession could alter the club's approach to the January window.

That is where Kroupi's situation becomes particularly interesting.

Bailey reports that PSG are admirers of the Bournemouth forward and that Doue's injury could encourage them to intensify an interest that existed well before Saturday's events.

Sources indicate that kroupi would not necessarily represent a direct replacement for Doue. Although capable of operating across the attacking line, he is primarily a centre-forward, meaning any move would also reflect a broader decision about how Enrique wishes to reshape his available options.

Sources indicate that there is currently no indication that PSG have opened negotiations with Bournemouth or made Kroupi their preferred January target. The possibility of an accelerated approach remains dependent on the club's assessment of its attacking needs.

For Arsenal, the prospect of renewed PSG interest adds another dimension to an already complicated transfer pursuit.

The Gunners have been following Kroupi's development for several months, while Tottenham have also been linked with the attacker. Barcelona and Bayern Munich are among the other European clubs reportedly keeping a close eye on his progress.

Industry observers note that kroupi's emergence has made him one of Bournemouth's most valuable assets. The former Lorient forward scored 13 Premier League goals last season and has since earned international recognition with France, strengthening his reputation as one of the country's most promising young attacking talents.

Recent findings suggest that however, Bournemouth are under little pressure to sanction an immediate sale. Kroupi remains under contract until June 2030, and the Cherries are determined to benefit from his performances during the remainder of the campaign.

David Ornstein recently indicated in The Athletic that a January transfer was unlikely, with Bournemouth expected to be more receptive to offers next summer. The journalist also suggested that the player could favour a move abroad when the time comes to leave the Vitality Stadium.

That possibility represents a further concern for Arsenal, particularly given PSG's existing interest and Kroupi's connections with French football.

Recent findings suggest that the financial demands are equally significant. Bournemouth have been linked with an asking price of at least £80m, although other reports have suggested that an even larger offer could be required to secure an agreement.

Those figures reflect the club's negotiating position rather than a confirmed bid from any interested party.

Arsenal's previously reported difficulties in securing a January deal therefore remain relevant regardless of whether PSG decide to make their interest more concrete.

A significant offer from Paris could potentially change the competitive landscape, particularly if the French champions decide that their injury problems justify an expensive winter investment.

Yet Bournemouth's position is unlikely to soften simply because another club has suffered an attacking setback. Any January approach would have to overcome the same contractual and financial obstacles facing Arsenal and Tottenham.

For now, PSG's growing need for attacking cover provides a newly introduced consideration in Kroupi's future, but the immediate question for all three interested clubs is whether Bournemouth can be persuaded to discuss a transfer before the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

It has been revealed that andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sources indicate that sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Recent findings suggest that diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Sources indicate that forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Sources indicate that few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that with a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Recent findings suggest that juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

It has been revealed that those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

“He took another step into the right direction. Very impressive and happy that he is on that route. Now he plays in Europe for Bournemouth and deserves to be with us.”.

That praise from their former manager will only increase Chelsea’s interest. Scott’s energy and composure suit the identity Xabi Alonso wants to build at Stamford Bridge. The Spaniard has already shown he is willing to rotate his squad, as seen in Xabi Alonso’s squad management decisions this season.

Chelsea travel to face Bournemouth in the Premier League soon. It is a fixture that will give Alonso a close look at a player repeatedly linked with his club. Build-up to that game is already underway, with team news arriving ahead of the Bournemouth clash.

According to recent reports, the prospects of an Alex Scott Chelsea transfer happening in January now look slim. Supporters hoping for fresh competition in central midfield may need patience, with Chelsea more likely to revisit their interest when the summer window opens.

Man United transfer news: Bruno Fernandes delivers massive update on contract talks amid AC Milan links

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 12:16.
  • Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has claimed that it is 'not the right moment' to be talking about a fresh contract at Old Trafford.
  • Fernandes will lead out the Red Devils against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, with Mauricio Pochettino looking to mark his arrival at Old Trafford with a statement win.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 12:16.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has claimed that it is 'not the right moment' to be talking about a fresh contract at Old Trafford.

Fernandes will lead out the Red Devils against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, with Mauricio Pochettino looking to mark his arrival at Old Trafford with a statement win.

Pochettino has confirmed that the Portuguese will remain as skipper, but reports emerged earlier this week that the playmaker is yet to accept an offer of a fresh deal.

Should Fernandes pen fresh terms at a time when Man United sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League table, it would represent a major boost for the club.

However, speaking in an interview with Sky Sports, Fernandes has suggested that he has no intention of committing his future to United anytime soon.

While Fernandes spoke positively over club officials making an attempt to extend his contract, he is keen to focus on matters on the pitch.

The former Sporting Lisbon star said: "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.

"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

Industry observers note that "I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.".

He added: "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season.

"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most vital thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.".

Unless Man United move clear of the Premier League relegation zone, it is highly unlikely that Fernandes will be signing a new contract.

That would make no sense for either party, regardless of Fernandes noted to have admirers in AC Milan, who are managed by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

United can activate a 12-month option to protect their position, and that feels like the most realistic development over the coming months.

Latest Update: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman.
  • "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful!
  • At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

Recent findings suggest that the two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second indicated his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Sources indicate that max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

According to recent reports, “A joy to have him,” stated Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

In a recent development, “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” mentioned Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

It has been revealed that arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

Sources indicate that the only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Sources indicate that ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

In a recent development, akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta mentioned: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

According to recent reports, asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

According to recent reports, he added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

Recent findings suggest that “Individually some substantial performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

According to recent reports, their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

According to recent reports, pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the fresh head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

Recent findings suggest that according to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

In a recent development, the Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

The defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical plan was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the issues exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

According to recent reports, pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

For Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.
  • It has been revealed that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect.
  • The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

It has been revealed that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

Sources indicate that the changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not presently planning to recruit a replacement.

West Ham failed to overcome bottom side Preston North End in what was a desperately disappointing spectacle for West Ham fans who had been expecting so much more from their upcoming manager’s first home game.

Industry observers note that A scrappy first goal conceded came from pretty much Preston’s only attempt at goal, and then our visitors sat back in time-honoured tradition. Four times the Hammers crashed the ball against the woodwork in a first half which indicated plenty of promise, however the second half evaporated in familiar fashion, inexplicably, no sooner than Mavropanos crashed in the equaliser.

Just about every fan expected West Ham to go on and win the game convincingly – yet instead they huffed and puffed with endless ‘after you – no after you’ short, sideways passes as nobody took responsibility for making the killer pass or – heaven forbid- taking on the shot.

However, the West Ham manager will no doubt do his best, tomorrow maybe, to pull out positives, despite being ‘devastated‘ at the result:.

It has been revealed that edson Álvarez, in his first game this season, El Machin was, surprisingly, up to speed pretty much immediately, sitting in front of the defence. He was everywhere: collecting, tidying up, harrying, attacking and breaking down opponents’ attacks. The late-tackling liability of last season was nowhere to be seen as he impressed and looks as if he has found himself a role for the coming weeks.

However, there’s a caveat: Remember this is the bottom side in the division who have just held us to draw. It will be intriguing to see if he copes against tougher opponents.

Edson Alvarez -Looked in control this afternoon – of his own discipline and of his midfield patch.

Finn Herrick: It can only have been unsettling, as the young keeper came to punch his first corner only to find a team mate’s glancing header got there first, looping the ball over his outstretched fists and allowing Preston to open the scoring against the run of play.

Sources indicate that credit to him, Herrick kept his cool and grew in stature as the game went on. He made an excellent double save after Mayers’ poor defensive header, and played well with the ball at his feet, combining Areola’s shot-stopping ability and Hermansen’s football skills.

However, positives aside, Parker has his work cut out simply to get this team’s work rate up. This time, they started quick and could have had three in the first half, even though there was a hesitancy and a lack of creation in front of goal.

It has been revealed that why it evaporated no sooner than the Hammers had equalised was a mystery. What should have become a barrage launched on Preston’s goal became a last thirty minutes of frustrating misfiring.

Just. Not. Good.Enough. Despite the bright points which Parker referenced in his post – match conference.

Just don’t blame West Ham’s newest manager for the failure of the last three to demand pacy, attacking football and recruiting so-called strikers who wouldn’t have made it into West Ham’s championships side of 2004/5 or 2011/12.

Sources indicate that can’t make a silk purse out of a sows ear. Especially not in two weeks.

  • West Ham United will travel to Fratton Park for the first time in 14 years for Tuesday's Championship clash against Portsmouth.
  • The Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in 10th place, while the hosts are a point behind in 12th spot in the Championship table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 22 Nov 2026 12:56, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:06.

West Ham United will travel to Fratton Park for the first time in 14 years for Tuesday's Championship clash against Portsmouth.

The Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in 10th place, while the hosts are a point behind in 12th spot in the Championship table.

Portsmouth are sitting four points adrift of the top eight after winning six, drawing five and losing five of their 16 league games this term.

Pompey put together a six-game unbeaten run before they fell to a narrow 2-1 defeat in their most recent home outing before the international break.

John Mousinho's side then returned to action with an underwhelming display in Saturday's 1-1 away draw against Bolton Wanderers, which saw Josh Murphy score the opener with what proved to be Pompey's only shot on target.

Murphy's first goal since March 2025 was soon called out by Sam Dalby as Portsmouth played out a third consecutive away draw after previously taking a point from trips to Wolverhampton Wanderers and Burnley.

Portsmouth will now return to the familiar surroundings of Fratton Park, where they have won four of their last six outings since losing their opening two home games.

That mentioned, they will be looking to tighten up their backline if they are to take anything off the league's highest scorers, having recorded just one clean sheet in their eight outings at Fratton Park.

Meanwhile, West Ham have significant work to do if they are to secure an immediate return to the Premier League in their first Championship campaign since 2011-12.

The West Ham hierarchy took the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after being underwhelmed by a return of six wins from the opening 13 league matches of the season.

Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken over the reins, but he is still waiting to secure his first win after over two draws and one defeat in his first three matches.

After starting his reign with a comeback 3-3 draw against Cardiff City, Parker saw his side fall to a narrow 2-1 loss against Blackburn Rovers, before his charges returned from the international break with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Championship's basement side Preston North End.

As a result, West Ham have now gone five games without a win since recording back-to-back away victories over Lincoln City and Swansea City, leaving them three points adrift of the playoff spots and eight points away from the top two.

In search of inspiration, the Hammers can take confidence from the fact they have already beaten Portsmouth at home in the EFL Cup this season, and have won two of their previous three head-to-head away games - a 4-1 success in December 2008 (a game that Parker started) and a 1-0 victory in January 2012.

West Ham United Championship form:.

Portsmouth’s lengthy absentee list features Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, Luke Brooke-Smith, Keshi Anderson, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Benjamin Arthur and Connor Ogilvie.

Jayden Meghoma is a doubt after being forced off in the closing stages against Bolton with an ankle problem, while a calf matter prevented Marlon Pack from starting Saturday’s draw.

Mousinho will welcome back midfielder Ebou Adams, who has served his one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Kyle Walker-Peters and Keiber LaMadrid due to muscle and knee problems respectively.

Goalkeeper Alphonse Areola remains a doubt after sitting out Saturday’s draw with an injury he sustained in the pre-match warm-up against Blackburn earlier this month.

Defender Max Kilman is expected to come into the back four after completing his one-match suspension for accumulating five yellow cards in the Championship.

Portsmouth possible starting lineup:.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Adams, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Kamara; Shade.

West Ham United possible starting lineup:.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Alvarez; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Taty.

While West Ham lost their last away game against Blackburn, that result represents their only defeat in their eight Championship road trips this season, so we expect them to take something from this midweek encounter.

However, we think they will be forced to settle for a point against a Portsmouth side that has lost just one of their previous eight matches.

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane has criticised the players’ performance and questioned supporters applauding them after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, insisting the early red card was no excuse for the manner of the loss.

It has been revealed that mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge unravelled when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes at Anfield. Liverpool scored twice inside 13 minutes and added two more goals after the break, leaving United 19th in the Premier League.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Keane challenged the suggestion that United’s performance was understandable because they had played most of the match with 10 men.

Sources indicate that “Fans are applauding. Applauding what?” he asked, before describing the performance as “rubbish”.

It has been revealed that keane argued that United should have shown greater fight and quality, claiming Liverpool could have scored eight or nine goals. He also questioned why responsibility for the club’s problems so often fell on managers, owners and executives rather than the players themselves.

Some travelling supporters applauded the team after the final whistle, potentially recognising the difficulty of playing more than 80 minutes with a numerical disadvantage. Keane, however, viewed the reaction as evidence of declining expectations.

It has been revealed that keane also challenged fellow former United captain Gary Neville, who had suggested the early dismissal made the result more understandable. Neville was far from satisfied with United’s performance, though, and separately accused the club’s hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen the defence.

Sources indicate that the disagreement reflected two concerns surrounding United: the players’ response to adversity and the quality of the squad available to Pochettino. Liverpool’s goals came from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the hosts creating numerous further opportunities.

In a recent development, pochettino defended his players’ commitment afterwards and questioned Yoro’s dismissal, arguing that Alexander Isak had not established control of the ball when the defender challenged him. United have taken just eight points from 11 Premier League matches, leaving their upcoming manager with little time to improve results. They travel to Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action.

Sources indicate that keane’s criticism adds to the scrutiny surrounding the squad following another heavy defeat to their fiercest rivals. For Pochettino, the immediate challenge is to improve defensive organisation while restoring confidence in a side struggling near the bottom of the table.

There will be no live UK television coverage of Chelsea’s return to Premier League action against Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.

Xabi Alonso’s side host the Cherries at Stamford Bridge in a traditional 3pm kick-off, with the fixture falling within the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

That means supporters unable to attend will need to follow the match through other channels, rather than watching it live on Sky Sports or TNT Sports.

Although the game will not be televised live in the UK, supporters can follow developments through the official Chelsea website and the Premier League website.

The Saturday 3pm blackout prevents live domestic television broadcasts during the restricted period, although overseas coverage may be available through broadcasters holding the relevant rights.

Highlights will be available after the match through the usual broadcast and digital channels, subject to their respective release schedules.

Chelsea will then turn their attention to a trip to Everton on Saturday, 17 October, with that fixture scheduled for a 12.30pm kick-off at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

For Alonso, the Bournemouth match provides the immediate opportunity to resume Chelsea’s domestic campaign following the international break.

West Ham 1-1 Preston: Scott Parker Still Struggling To Unlock Jarrod Bowen

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that west Ham were nowhere near good enough against the worst team in the division.
  • Edson Álvarez looked decent enough on his return to the team, but Scott Parker looks no closer to getting the best out of Jarrod Bowen than Nuno Espírito Santo or Graham Potter did.
  • It has been revealed that the statistics certainly make for interesting reading.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that west Ham were nowhere near good enough against the worst team in the division. Whilst we had our chances, it would be a long stretch to suggest we were significantly better than Preston, particularly during a first half in which the visitors created opportunities of their own.

Edson Álvarez looked decent enough on his return to the team, but Scott Parker looks no closer to getting the best out of Jarrod Bowen than Nuno Espírito Santo or Graham Potter did. In essence, the Hammers lacked magic, and watching our best player pinned to the right flank was depressing.

It has been revealed that the statistics certainly make for interesting reading. West Ham registered 30 attempts on goal, but only four were on target. We also hit the woodwork three times, with Bowen and Joël Veltman striking opposite posts during the same passage of play before Edvin Austbø rattled the crossbar shortly after half-time.

Preston took the lead through Liam Lindsay after just 18 minutes, following a corner which Joël Piroe inadvertently flicked towards his own goal.

Konstantinos Mavropanos eventually equalised on the hour mark, heading home Arne Engels’ cross after Manor Solomon had helped create the opening.

Yet even after drawing level, West Ham couldn’t find a winner against a team who arrived at the London Stadium bottom of the Championship.

There were chances, certainly. Tomáš Souček had a late header tipped over, while Mavropanos headed over in stoppage time. But for all the possession and pressure, there was precious little composure in front of goal.

And as far as I’m concerned, this was a match West Ham simply had to win.

What makes the situation particularly frustrating is that we’ve already seen what Bowen can do when he’s given more freedom.

Industry observers note that during the remarkable comeback against Cardiff City, our captain was allowed to drift into central positions, where he caused all sorts of problems. His movement, passing and ability to find space helped transform a game which had looked completely lost at half-time.

I was so impressed that I subsequently wrote about how Scott Parker needed to restore West Ham’s most dangerous weapon.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, against Blackburn, Bowen was back operating as a conventional right winger. And against Preston, we saw much the same thing.

That’s not to suggest Bowen didn’t contribute. He was involved throughout and managed eight attempts on goal, including the effort which struck the post.

But there’s a difference between getting Bowen involved in the game and getting the best out of him.

West Ham have spent far too long relying on our captain to produce something special from wide positions, often with defenders able to anticipate where he’s going to receive the ball.

Against Cardiff, we briefly saw something different.

Bowen was the inspiration behind that second-half recovery. He looked far more dangerous when he was able to move into the middle and influence the game rather than remaining tied to the touchline.

I genuinely thought Parker had stumbled upon something which could change West Ham’s season.

Instead, two matches later, we seem to have gone backwards.

Of course, the manager has plenty of other challenges demanding his attention.

Industry observers note that there were some positives against Preston. Álvarez made his first Championship appearance for West Ham since May 2025 and looked reasonably comfortable in midfield, while young goalkeeper Finlay Herrick produced an excellent double save to prevent the visitors doubling their lead.

Mavropanos also deserves credit for another important goal, particularly given that he is a centre-back who continues to contribute at the other end of the pitch.

But the bigger picture remains deeply concerning.

West Ham simply had to start turning the London Stadium into somewhere opposition teams feared visiting.

Instead, the bottom club have come away with a point, and Parker has now overseen two draws and a defeat in his first three matches.

I appreciate he hasn’t been in the job long, and I’m not suggesting he’s solely responsible for problems which have been developing for some considerable time.

However, the international break gave him an opportunity to work with the players, and I had hoped to see considerably more improvement than we witnessed.

For me, the biggest concern remains our inability to get the best out of Bowen.

Recent findings suggest that we have a player capable of providing the creativity, movement and unpredictability that this team so desperately needs. Yet we’re still asking him to spend most of his time playing in the same predictable areas of the pitch.

In a recent development, west Ham don’t lack effort. Against Preston, they certainly didn’t lack possession or attempts on goal.

And until Scott Parker finds a way of giving Jarrod Bowen the freedom to provide it, I fear we’re going to see plenty more afternoons like this one.

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

Recent findings suggest that according to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

Sources indicate that “To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he stated, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher remarked.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

Industry observers note that united host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.

Slovan Bratislava will be looking to secure their first victory of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign when they host Real Betis at Tehelne Pole Stadion on Tuesday.

The Sky Blues sit bottom of the league phase table with no points from four matches, while Betis occupy 11th place with nine points.

Slovan defeated Celje away from home in the second leg of their playoff-round tie to secure a place in the Champions League main phase, marking a historic achievement for the club.

However, the Slovakian side have found the step up in quality difficult to handle, losing all four of their matches, scoring just once and conceding 17 goals.

Yaya Toure's side began their campaign with a heavy 6-1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain before suffering further losses against Stuttgart, Roma and LASK.

Balancing their domestic and European commitments has also proved challenging, with their continental struggles seemingly affecting their league form, as they sit second in the Slovakian top flight, seven points behind leaders DAC 1904 despite having played a game more.

Perhaps most frustrating for Toure is Slovan's poor home form, with the Sky Blues winless in their last five matches at Tehelne Pole Stadion, drawing three of those encounters.

Real Betis have made a solid start to their European campaign, collecting three wins from four matches while scoring eight goals and conceding six.

El Glorioso opened their campaign with a hard-fought 3-2 victory over Lille, coming from behind to claim all three points.

They followed that up with another thrilling 3-2 win against Porto before beating Feyenoord 1-0 to secure back-to-back home victories.

Manuel Pellegrini's side suffered a narrow 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in their previous Champions League outing, but they have an excellent opportunity to climb the table with a victory over Slovan.

Betis are unbeaten in their last three matches across all competitions and head into this encounter on the back of a 1-1 draw against city rivals Sevilla in La Liga.

Artur Gajdos appeared to pick up an injury in the previous game and could be replaced by Alexej Maros, while Andraz Sporar is set to continue up front, with Roman Cerepaki a doubt due to a back problem.

That eight point gap between West Ham United in tenth and the Championship front runners is starting to look mighty huge with just sixteen games completed.

Of course the reality is that there are still thirty games remaining but West Ham will have to find a way of converting all the huffing and puffing into points or else we will find ourselves scratching around even trying to make the enlarged play off places come May next year.

“Wasteful West Ham”: Not my words but the description on the official club web site which sums up perfectly an afternoon of toil and frustration against the bottom side in the league.

Industry observers note that scott Parker pronounced himself happy with the effort, if ‘bitterly disappointed’ with the result. As were we all.

The team announcement produced a wave of optimism, and I’m not sure yet that we should ditch that: Tenth place is not where we expected to be at the end of November but there is still plenty of time to turn the West Ham supertanker back on course and away from the rocky peril of mid table, second division mediocrity.

But three years’ decline won’t be fixed in three games.

Introducing Fin Herrick and Edson Alvarez were bold decisions which could have backfired totally, especially after the maddening concession in the first half. Now Scott Parker needs to keep his nerve and persevere with that set up, go again on Tuesday night away at Fratton Park and trust for better luck and better finishing.

Ninety points still up for grabs this season, Hammers.

In a recent development, at least the ownership saw fit to ditch Nuno in time to turn the ship around. In the bad old days of David Sullivan, we’d still be on about game 5 of 20 ‘must win’ games before Nuno had to walk the plank. (Not sure where all the nautical terms came from this morning).

Industry observers note that in any case, there’s not another manager who’d do any better in Scott Parker’s place right now. Don’t panic. Yet. COYI!

  • It could have been something different.
  • “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that they scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, revealed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

It has been revealed that THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Sources indicate that yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

Industry observers note that rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Significant save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Industry observers note that pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

In a recent development, his touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

It has been revealed that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some crucial saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Industry observers note that spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo remarked.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

It was a better performance. On another day, they could have had two or three goals. Liverpool just had enough.”.

Mac Allister takes but his effort is off target. That is indeed the final moment of the half and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of that fine Mac Allister strike.

Industry observers note that marmoush is the first Tottenham player booked tonight for a foul on McConnell and that feels on the harsh side. Definitely a foul but was it a yellow?

That is a dreadful decision from referee Andy Madley. Frimpong gets the better of Tel in a contest down Tottenham’s left, with the former outmuscling the latter. Not only is Frimpong penalised, he is booked.

Mac Allister spurns a glorious chance to get his and Liverpool’s second of the night. Tottenham again risk it at the back and lose it. Industry observers note that liverpool want a penalty. Tottenham give it away cheaply inside their own box and McConnell goes down under a challenge from Senesi, who was the one who gave it away. Araujo is then booked for pulling Marmoush back.

There is no way Tottenham’s goal drought will last in perpetuity but they have missed two fabulous chances so far and you wonder what impact that will have on their confidence. At least one Tottenham player is being feted: Andy Robertson, who has just jogged down the touchline at Anfield in a different kit for the first time in nine years. He tried not to acknowledge the singing of his name too much but you could see it meant something to him.

The home fans serenade their former player Robertson as the now Tottenham left-back goes out to warm up.

That is a big chance for Kudus to equalise on the counter. Tottenham break from deep inside their own half and charge down their left. Bergvall waits for Udogie to come on the overlap before playing the pass. From the left side of the box, Udogie crosses for Kudus, who gets across the front of Kerkez. Kudus should probably score but lifts his effort over the bar from just six yards out.

That was a chance for Udogie. Senesi clips in a lovely ball over the top in behind to pick out the run from left-back of Udogie, who tries to chest it down but cannot keep it under control. Had he done so, it would have been a great chance.

The way Alexis Mac Allister has played this past fortnight, anyone would think he is trying to secure himself a newly introduced contract. All cynicism aside, that was a quite beautiful goal and attention must be drawn to Cody Gakpo’s involvement: he took a pass on his chest from Joe Gomez before opening up the pitch. We will say it again: the idea of selling Gakpo in the last window was madness.

Recent findings suggest that he scored a stunner nearly a week ago against Atletico Madrid here in the Champions League and he adds another storming strike to his repertoire. The ball finds kindly to Mac Allister on the edge of the box after Udogie tackled Ngumoha and the Argentine finds the top corner with a first-time finish.

“He has got to fit that jigsaw puzzle together. There are still a lot of elements that are not right; they have not got a left-sided player they can trust in. Goals have been a real problem, but I do think they will come.”.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

Sources indicate that “I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola mentioned. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no problems. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is fresh, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

In a recent development, liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

According to recent reports, tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have substantial confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I stated we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

Recent findings suggest that as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that the Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

In a recent development, amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That shows in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

The shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

According to recent reports, in the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

According to recent reports, the Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

Industry observers note that everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A).

Milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

On that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having stated all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

Industry observers note that just over one year ago, West Ham’s Finlay Herrick was stepping out on loan for Boreham Wood in the National League – the fifth tier of English football. A far cry from London Stadium yesterday as he replaced Mads Hermansen in goal and made his Championship debut, apparently hearing about his impending start just on the morning of the game.

And despite the first half concession from the corner, Herrick did a pretty fair job with excellent double saves later in the game and some assured glove work catching the ball – which had seemed like a lost art at times in the last couple of years.

Herrick after his unforgettable FA Cup penalty shootout debut last year.

According to recent reports, this was a massive gamble by Scott Parker which could have backfired dreadfully. With no Areola, the temptation must have been to revert to Hermansen yet the Hammers’ head coach stuck with his instinct. After the first half goal concession, Parker must have wondered – briefly – whether he’d made a huge howler.

Has Herrick done enough to keep his place? It seems Parker is dead set on replacing Hermansen so until Alphonse Areola is ‘fit and ready’ then Herrick should be prepared for more pitch time. He certainly has the ambition:.

According to recent reports, “I hope this is the start. I hope I’ve done myself justice and proved to the fans that I don’t just want to be third choice, I want to be playing, I want to get back to the Premier League and be part of that”. (whu/youtube).

Describing the competition amongst the trio of goal keepers, Herrick was quick to praise Hermansen for the encouragement and help he’s received recently, describing the three keepers as a team more than individuals fighting amongst themselves for the sole starting spot:.

“There’s one goal keeper shirt and there’s three of us – but we’re like a band of brothers and we always stick together, me Mads and Fonz- no matter what. “.

Difficult to believe Herrick is still only 20 – he seems to have been around West Ham’s fringes for ever- but he joined the academy at six years old and looks to have the talent to go all the way. From yesterday’s solid start, he didn’t let his manager or his team mates down and should feel rightly pretty proud of himself.

The question for Scott Parker is whether he continues between the sticks at Fratton Park on Tuesday night.

As I left the London Stadium to a chorus of boos, I found myself desperately searching for positives from a frustrating 1-1 draw against the league’s bottom club.

Industry observers note that the first was the performance of Alvarez. Largely cast into the shadows through the stubbornness of our former manager, he grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck. He took control, lifted the crowd, and, above all, displayed the leadership qualities this team has lacked for much of the season.

It has been revealed that the second positive was that the statistics backed up what I’d watched unfold on the pitch. West Ham dominated possession with 79%, registered 30 shots, and recorded an xG of 3.13. The problem? Only four of those efforts were shots on target.

We gifted Preston their opening goal. It came from a calamitous mix-up, with Piroe’s flicked header looping backwards onto the crossbar before dropping kindly for Liam Lindsay to tap home from close range. It could be argued that Herrick should have been more commanding from the corner, but he made amends later with an excellent double save.

There were concerns that we wouldn’t pull one back, we did on the 60th minute, Mavropanos heading home his sixth goal in 15 league appearances this season.

“Ifs” and “buts” don’t win football matches, and as Parker said afterwards: “The overall performance suggests we should win. The fine margins of football are, and the reality is, if Tomas Soucek scores that last-minute goal, it’s probably a different interview.”.

In a recent development, for me, I’m not going to be negative. We needed a win and we didn’t get the three points, but what I want to see now is the team build on the domination, the chance creation and the shot volume by going to Fratton Park on Tuesday and getting the job done. If we concede first there and deliver an abject performance, then and only then will there be more serious questions to ask.

Recent findings suggest that yesterday was a bizarre and surreal experience at the London Stadium as we watched West Ham’s half-hearted attempts to beat a stubborn Preston North End side. Sure, the Hammers had 30 shots and an impressive 79% slice of the possession pie. But scratch below the surface and there are still big problems with Scott Parker’s team, some of which I suspect will not be sorted out until the January transfer window.

Despite West Ham’s impressive array of shots, passes and corners, I never truly felt that the team had the magic or the cutting edge to win the game. And as crazy as it sounds, considering we’d hit the post twice and had 14 corners, I don’t actually think we threatened enough. The Hammers lacked sparkle and magic, for sure.

Alvarez- first game back in claret and blue for a year and a half.

Sources indicate that edson Álvarez was an excellent addition to the team, but he is a defensive midfielder, and realistically, the defence was improved. Herrick made a bit of a blooper in goal for the opener, but I felt he redeemed himself with an excellent double save. By and large, West Ham restricted Preston’s chances, and so we should have done. After all, they’re the worst team in the division.

It has been revealed that but our biggest problems came in attack. Edvin Austbø on the left wing flattered to deceive, cutting inside and shooting just off target at one point, but never really terrorising his marker, despite the fact that he had him on a yellow card. Joël Piroe did okay but fluffed his major chance when put through by Arne Engels.

As for the supply line, Divine Mukasa flitted in and out of the game and did not create anywhere near enough, given his deployment in the number 10 position. Jarrod Bowen was wide. I mean, very wide for so much of the game that he was probably on first-name terms with the linesman. But realistically, he was just out of the game for large parts of it. We’ll get into more detail on that later.

Overall, it was nowhere near enough quality. Sure, we had momentum. Sure, we had possession. But this did not look like a group of Premier League-standard players against the worst team in the division.

Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
